  >=50% of the request budget; a timeout on a RESPONSIVE loop is still fully
  charged, so real outage detection is unweakened. 5 tests, the regression one

2026-09-07 01:45 | Bay | hypothesis: the entry funnel does not stop at a GATE
  at all -- 66% of candidates die with no refusal row, so the loss is
  upstream of every gate that has been audited |
  did: (1) per-symbol 6h funnel from trading_ops -- 182 candidates across 43
  symbols, but only 9 symbols ever reach an entry-gate outcome; 120 of 182
  candidate rows (66%) have NO entry and NO refusal. (2) Found the terminal
  state: TradingScheduler.evaluate returns None at scheduler.py:821 setting
  state.last_filter_reason = "no_candidates (thresholds not met)", which is
  written to no table. (3) Read it out of organism_snapshots.scheduler
  instead: 379 of 532 route evaluations in 6h (71%) end there. (4) Walked the
  enter branch: it needs direction_prob >= SCHEDULER_MIN_DIRECTION_PROB (0.6).
  Measured 530 evaluations in 6h -- max EXACTLY 0.5000, so 0/530.
  result: CONFIRMED, and the cause is a SCALE error, not a threshold.
  Over 3007 paired evaluations in 72h:
      model's own output (direction_prob_raw)   median 0.5985  max 0.9498
      what the decision path saw                median 0.1414  max 0.7183
      >= 0.58 (bot.py enter_threshold)          16/3007 = 0.53%
      >= 0.60 (SCHEDULER_MIN_DIRECTION_PROB)    15/3007 = 0.50%
      read as BEARISH (< 0.5)                 2910/3007 = 96.8%
  The model is bullish just over half the time; the decision path reads it as
  bearish 96.8% of the time. Fitting the transform on the 1324 evals where
  graph_confidence was EXACTLY 1.0 (nothing else touching the number) gives
      logit_out = 0.9806 * logit_in - 2.0784   median |resid| 0.048
  i.e. the active model's Platt calibration, whose no-information point is
  sigmoid(-2.0784) = 0.111, NOT 0.5. Clearing the 0.58 entry gate needs a raw
  model output of 0.906. Every threshold reading direction_prob was chosen
  against a 0.5-neutral scale and services/env_loader.py says so out loud --
  it pins MONEY_BUTTON_MIN_DIR_PROB to "0.50" with the comment "so the
  neutral case PASSES".
  SHIPPED, both halves of the same units error, in trading/bot.py:
   * _summarise_predictions: re-centre on the calibrator's own neutral point
     (subtract cal_offset on the logit scale). The offset carries the BASE
     RATE, the scale carries the sharpening; a threshold asking "more bullish
     than no information" wants the base rate divided out and the sharpening
     kept. Identity when cal_offset is 0. True P(up) still published as
     direction_prob_calibrated.
   * damp_direction_prob(): was `direction_prob * graph_conf`, a probability
     multiplied by a confidence. It can only LOWER the number (graph_conf
     p25 = 0.80 over 707 evals) and it moves toward 0 = "certainly down"
     instead of toward 0.5 = "no opinion". A bullish 0.62 at graph_conf 0.80
     came out at 0.496 -- sign flipped on a confidence discount alone. It also
     capped direction_prob at graph_conf, so a 0.80 tick could never clear
     0.58 at ANY model output.
  Replayed over the same 3007 real evaluations, gate input:
      median          0.1414 -> 0.5818   (model raw median 0.5985)
      >= 0.58          0.53% -> 50.12%
      >= 0.60          0.50% -> 47.12%
      reads bearish     96.8% -> 35.6%
  14 tests. Verified failing against the old code both ways: reverting the
  calibration block fails 3, mutating the helper back to `prob * conf` fails
  4. One test reads _interpret_predictions.__code__.co_names, because a
  concurrent stale-buffer write to bot.py reverted the CALL SITE mid-pass
  while leaving the helper in place and every arithmetic test still passed.
  next: production must be RESTARTED to pick this up (it booted 00:53 on the
  old code). Then re-measure, in order: (a) organism_snapshots direction_prob
  median -- expect ~0.58, not 0.14; (b) the share of route evaluations ending
  at "no_candidates" -- expect well under 71%; (c) ghost entries/24h -- 14 now,
  and 12 more fresh atf_static ghost round trips is the whole re-arm bar.
  Second, unshipped finding, worth its own pass: "no_candidates (thresholds
  not met)" is the single largest terminal state in the funnel and writes NO
  trading_ops row, which is the only reason this took a snapshot join to find.

- 2026-09-07 Sage. HYPOTHESIS: the omen wall is the TARGET, not the
  representation -- three passes moved train recall 89.2 -> 98.7% by fixing

  DID: built trading/omen_path.py (path-dependent take/stop labelling),
  scripts/omen_label_audit.py and scripts/omen_barrier_sweep.py; walked
  294,241 bars x 12 hourly corpora and 94,714 bars x 10 five-minute corpora,
  offline, no node, nothing retrained. Then followed the arithmetic into the
  cost constant and shipped services/round_trip_cost.py.
  RESULT:
  (1) MY 'murk hides fast winners' HALF IS WRONG. Of 120,775 murk bars,
  29.29% are path wins and 31.80% are path stops -- net -2.51%. Murk is
  near-random. Dropped.
  (2) THE OTHER HALF IS REAL: 30.57% of the bars the endpoint label calls a
  BUY hit the stop before the target. Nearly a third of what the brain is
  taught to want is a realised loss once a stop exists.
  (3) THE LAW. break-even p* = (S+c)/(T+S), and indiscriminate entry on a
  driftless price already gives p0 = S/(T+S), so THE SKILL A SELECTOR MUST
  ADD IS EXACTLY c/(T+S) -- cost over barrier width, and nothing else. Not
  volatility, not horizon, not symbol. Corollary: EVERY barrier pair has
  exactly zero pre-cost expectancy, so barriers alone can never pay and a
  symmetric take/stop is a guaranteed donation of the fee. At the omen's own

judge it on gross-versus-cost, not on net or on hit rate.

THE REAL FIX IS LIMIT DISCIPLINE, AND NOTHING IN THIS CODEBASE DOES IT YET.
A simulated resting order cannot fill better than its own limit:

    take-profit ->  book min(price, target_price)
    stop        ->  book max(price, stop_price)

AND THE FRAMING MATTERS FOR WHERE IT GOES. It is not "live has a guard and
ghost does not". The LIVE lane cannot manufacture this at all, because its
fill is a real swap receipt. The GHOST lane is a SIMULATION that credits
itself the entire gap through its own limit. So the fix belongs on the ghost
booking path, not in a shared sanity helper.

(stop_loss:-0.1415 on CP-USDC). 4 of 13 fill worse than 0.970, worth -0.1780
of the -0.6094 stop total. THE BIAS IS NOT SYMMETRIC: the take-profit side
overshoots WITHOUT BOUND (+2.5680) and the stop side is bounded by the
position (-0.1780). An unguarded fill does not average out -- it biases the
ghost book UPWARD, which is the direction that graduates strategies.

### 2026-09-10 pass 102 -- Iris -- the stale exit had never fired, and a zero is not a clock

**Hypothesis going in (my own, filed as [71975c13] last pass):** positions
outlive `stale_exit_secs` because exits are evaluated only when a tick arrives,
so the fix is a wall-clock sweep. **I had already half-corrected this at the end
of pass 100** (1112 post-stale ticks closed nothing) and this pass finished the
correction with the number that settles it.

**What I did:** counted the reason on every logged ghost exit rather than
reasoning about the chain. Over 7d, all 206 rows of `trading_ops` status
`ghost-exit`:

    max_hold 52 | target_hit 16 | stop_loss 5 | stale_underwater 4
    timed-exit 0 | confidence_drop 0 | negative_margin 0

**RESULT: rule 4 had never once produced an outcome, and `max_hold` -- the 3600s
eviction, 4x the 900s promise -- is the biggest named exit reason.** A slow clock
cannot produce a zero; an unreachable branch can.

**Mechanism.** `confidence_drop`/`negative_margin` fire at `MIN_HOLD_SECONDS`
(300s) and sat ABOVE `timed-exit` (900s) in one elif chain at bot.py:7463. An
elif that fires CONSUMES the tick, so any position past the stale clock the
model was bearish about resolved to `confidence_drop`, leaving rule 4 reachable
only for a position the model felt exactly NEUTRAL about. Production is not that
state -- median `direction_prob` 0.2560, 68.6% of 1050 decisions below the 0.45
floor. And the names are not interchangeable downstream: the ghost exit gate at
bot.py:9871 ADMITS `timed-exit` by name (`stale_verdict`) and REFUSES
`confidence_drop` at `economic_profit <= 0` as `hold-negative`, returning
without booking. So the stale loser was refused every tick for the whole
900s-3600s window until the eviction freed its slot booking nothing.

**Fix (1cc2a6a):** `timed-exit` moved above the two opinion rules. Narrow by
construction -- it can only change a position that satisfies its own condition
(past the clock AND not covering its round trip). Live unchanged: all three
reasons are outside `PROTECTIVE_REASONS`, so the live margin gate cannot tell
them apart; only the ghost gate does, deliberately.

**Why the existing test missed it:** `test_a_stale_loser_is_measured_not_forecast`
ticks at `direction_prob 0.5` and says so in its own comment -- "model_neutral,
which is what shuts off rules 3a and 3b. Without that this test would pass on
the wrong rule." It pinned rule 4 in the one model state where nothing outranks
it. New file ticks it bearish; 2 of its 3 tests fail against the pre-fix file.

**Not done, and the next pass must not mark it done:** there is still no
wall-clock sweep, so a fully dark symbol is still only evaluated on tick
arrival. And criteria 2/3 need POST-fix evidence -- **production is live and
ticking but still running the old `trading/bot.py`**, so re-running
`hold_time_edge.py` today measures the pre-fix book.

**Next:** confirm production restarted onto 1cc2a6a, then re-count exit reasons.
If `max_hold` stops being top and `timed-exit` goes non-zero, the fix is
carrying; the dark-feed sweep is a separate smaller item. Generalisable lesson:
**when a rule's outcome count is exactly zero, stop tuning its threshold and ask
what consumes its tick first.**

## 2026-09-10 — Iris, pass 104 — the pool's only wall clock was gated on a model buffer

**Hypothesis carried in from pass 103 (MINE, and it was wrong):** that the
wall-clock exit sweep [79ad4d0d] did not exist and had to be BUILT — in
`trading/selector.py`, over `self.bots`, priced by an on-chain quote. I spent
pass 103 unable to touch `trading/bot.py` and wrote that plan up as the
shortest path.

**What I actually found:** the sweep already exists.
`_abandon_dark_feed_positions` and `_exit_dark_live_positions` are called from
`_handle_sample` and fire on **any** symbol's tick by design — which makes them
the only pool-wide wall clock the exit rules have. The defect was *where they
sat in the method*: below the window gate (`len(self._buffer) < self.window_size`)
and below the duplicate-`(symbol, ts)` return. Neither has anything to do with
whether some *other* symbol's position has gone dark, and the sweep never
invokes the model — it reads `self.positions` and the shared tick map.

**Worst case, which is the one that matters:** a bot added by `reconcile_pairs`
*for a held symbol* — added precisely so that position can be closed — starts
with an EMPTY buffer and had to fill a full 60-step window before it would
sweep anything. At CBBTC-USDC's measured 50 ticks/h that is over an **hour** of
pool-wide clock lost, during which every dark position in the merged book waits
it out.

**Result:** shipped `edd0a88`. Gate 621 → **627 passed / 0 failed**,
`profit_logic_audit` NO KNOWN LOSING SHAPES. Moved, not weakened — no
threshold, horizon or guard changed. Proven by
`tests/test_a_dark_symbols_position_is_still_closed_on_its_clock.py`: a
HIGH-USDC position with ZERO ticks on its own symbol, swept from a *different*
symbol's tick. Both tests **fail against pre-fix `bot.py`**, verified by
stashing it rather than assuming.

**The transferable lesson:** the comment on that block already *asserted* the
property the code did not have — "the tick was recorded above the window gate
— see there for why" — while the block itself was below it. `_note_symbol_tick`
was hoisted for exactly this reason and the sweep was not hoisted with it. This
repo keeps shipping comments that describe the intended code rather than the
code, so the tests assert on behaviour, never on the log line or the comment.

**What I would try next:** criterion 2 of [79ad4d0d] — make the sweep *book* an
outcome instead of only freeing the slot. Do NOT reprice from the feed's last
tick: the reaper's docstring is right that an hours-old mark is the AERO +161%
artifact `StrategyLedger._is_implausible` exists to reject. The live lane
already solves this honestly — `_queue_forced_live_exit(..., reason="dark_feed")`
at `bot.py:~12085`, "Selling at the chain price". Reuse that for ghost.

### 2026-09-10 -- Gale, pass 107, addendum: THE HORIZON IS BELOW THE COST FLOOR

HYPOTHESIS: I closed the head question with "the skill does not survive cost"
and then asked the obvious next one, which nobody had: can a short horizon clear
the round trip AT ALL on this feed, independent of any model?

DID: added --horizon-table to scripts/head_vs_realised_census.py (187f0d9) and
swept horizons over 24h, ~5000 matched ticks each, against the receipt-measured
0.3187% of notional + 0.004047 fixed.

  horizon      n   median|ret|%   %ticks>cost   mean|ret|%   perfect-oracle net%
      5min   5108       0.0456         16.2%      0.1995            -0.1192
     10min   5297       0.0794         21.9%      0.2823            -0.0364
     15min   4984       0.1164         27.3%      0.3385            +0.0198
     30min   4873       0.2051         39.4%      0.5222            +0.2035
     60min   4364       0.3898         55.0%      0.8802            +0.5615
    120min   3855       0.7499         67.5%      1.5809            +1.2622

RESULT: THE LAST COLUMN IS A CEILING NOBODY CAN REACH -- direction called right
on every tick, whole move captured, cost paid once -- AND AT 5 AND 10 MINUTES IT
IS STILL NEGATIVE. No head, strategy or allocation fix makes those horizons pay;
the move is smaller than the toll. The MEDIAN is the honest row (the mean is
skew-inflated by a few large movers) and the median tick clears 0.3187% at no
horizon below roughly 45 minutes. So the TYPICAL trade loses to cost even with a
perfect direction call at every horizon this system currently targets.

This is a direct measured finding against the standing instruction "trade on the
scale of minutes -- single-digit to tens of minutes". On this feed at this cost,
the single-digit end is arithmetically unprofitable. It also explains the
graduation wall from a direction with nothing to do with the model: the whole
population is being asked to win a game whose entry fee exceeds the prize, which
is consistent with every strategy's tradeable P/L being negative or zero.

NO KNOB CHANGED, and I am deliberately NOT proposing to lengthen the horizon --
that is the operator's call, filed as [15cc71d4]. Two honest responses: accept a
30-60 min horizon and give up "minutes", or cut the 0.3187%. Only the second
preserves the stated goal. At $23.18 deployable the fixed leg adds ~0.017% more.

CAVEAT, not hidden: 24h of ONE flat-to-down tape. A calmer or wilder regime
moves every row, and [15cc71d4]'s second criterion asks for an UP window before
anyone bets on it.

NEXT: re-run --horizon-table over an UP window. If the 5/10-minute ceiling is

  minutes and sample repeatedly; a negative result inside one drain interval is

## 2026-09-10 pass 108 -- Cove -- the held-out window could not be MOVED

HYPOTHESIS: the brain's standing acceptance rule -- held-out edge in an UP window AND
a DOWN window, measured back-to-back on ONE fabric -- was not merely unmet, it was
unreachable with the instrument we had. Nothing was dealt to me this pass, so I took
the part of [cd461b30] its owner had not claimed: the comparator.

WHAT I FOUND, in scripts/omen_experiment.py, four lines of arithmetic:
    test_stop  = len(bars) - horizon - 1     # ALWAYS the end of the corpus
    train_stop = test_start - horizon        # moves when the test moves
Every run that has ever been done on this harness scored the LAST --test bars. A second
window was unreachable. And had anyone reached it, the training window would have moved
with it -- so the two windows would have been scored against two DIFFERENT training
sets. That is two experiments, not two measurements of one fabric, and their difference
would have measured the training data rather than the thing under test. Given that node
run-to-run variance already gave 89.2% and 93.6% on the same fabric 34 minutes apart,
this would have manufactured a difference and attributed it to a topology change.

WHAT I SHIPPED (e43add1, pushed, gate green, 9 new tests):
  --test-end      select the held-out window
  --train-end     PIN the training window across it
  --list-windows  census every candidate window with its up-rate and drift
  plan_windows()  pure arithmetic, so the load-bearing property is testable with no node

RESULT -- THE CENSUS, and it is the finding of the pass. AERO-USDC, 21926 bars, 400-bar
windows, horizon 12:
    test_end 21913  DOWN  up-rate 47.2%  mean fwd +0.0505%  <- the ONLY window reachable before
    test_end 21713  DOWN  up-rate 40.5%  mean fwd -0.4170%
    test_end 21113  UP    up-rate 53.8%  mean fwd +0.7592%
    test_end 20913  UP    up-rate 57.2%  mean fwd +1.1568%
The corpus is overwhelmingly DOWN and the UP windows are NOT at the end of it. The 47.2%
reproduces pass 107's reported up-rate exactly, so the instrument agrees with the
measurement it situates -- and it shows pass 107's "one DOWN window" was not a choice.

A DEFECT MY OWN FIXTURE CAUGHT, worth carrying beyond the brain: the window classifier
first scored up-rate over ALL forwards, so a window where price NEVER MOVED read up-rate
0.0 and was labelled DOWN. A frozen feed republishing one price would have been reported
as a down market -- and this repo has shipped frozen feeds, once with 82 of 94 symbols
holding a seed price. Zero-move bars are now excluded from the rate, the stalled share is
reported, and a window more than half stalled is FLAT whatever its live bars did.

NO EDGE CLAIMED, none measured. This is the instrument, not a result.
OMEN_STRATEGY_ENABLED untouched and still 0.

VERIFIED TWO-WINDOW PROTOCOL for whoever measures next -- one training set, disjoint
windows, fabric never saw either:

THE CLIENT IS HONEST, which is the good news: trading/omen_brain.py:_consolidate retries
a backpressured sample WIZARD_BACKPRESSURE_RETRIES (default 30) times at 2s and then
counts it in failed_pairs, never trained_pairs. No run reports frames it did not bind.
But 30 retries x 2s x TWO stages is up to 120 SECONDS PER SAMPLE, which is exactly how a
run looks alive while moving nothing.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN 8c86138 FROM PASS 107, and it should be discounted by whoever reads
it. I reported "the with-relations arm trains 3.3x slower, 1.7/s vs 5.6/s, because 10
collections train slower than 7". Backpressure retries produce precisely that signature,
and an arm that runs while another agent's node holds memory is slowed by the BOX, not
by its collection count. I did not record free RAM during that run so I cannot separate
the two. The honest position is that the 3.3x is UNEXPLAINED, not explained, and no
topology decision should rest on it.

WHAT THE NEXT PASS SHOULD DO FIRST, before any brain hypothesis: check free physical
memory against the 4096 MB floor and kill unused omen nodes. A brain result measured
under backpressure is not a weak result, it is not a result -- the fabric never learned
the samples the report says it was taught. This may also be part of why held-out numbers
here sit at chance, and it is a cheaper thing to rule out than a topology change.

RESULT: instrument shipped and proven (e43add1, 9 tests). Two-window baseline NOT
measured; filed as [47d70b7c] with the verified protocol so the next pass starts at the
measurement rather than at the harness. Jet separately verified kind='Internal' is a
NO-OP on this node, so no topology experiment was available this pass either.

OPERATOR-REPORTED, step 1 of his order of work, in my file, two lines. Fixed in 6be5357.

another.

were NEVER QUERIED. The query set could not move, so the arms could not differ. Any
experiment that changes WHICH collections discriminate was unfalsifiable on this harness.

order -- measured ('geometry','temporal','cross') against default
('temporal','geometry','cross'). Invisible until a change makes the measured set
genuinely different, and then it eats the change.

FIRING with its source; the report records what ACTUALLY fired plus query_source.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING, and it is the same shape as the backpressure finding above: this
repo's expensive bugs are the ones where the instrument REPORTS one thing and DOES
another, so the run looks healthy and the number means nothing. Two in one pass, from
different causes, both invisible to every check anyone was running. Verify the seam, not
the function.

HYPOTHESIS: the L1 co-occurrence motif layer abstracts (distinctness falls
L0->L1), and that abstraction carries held-out buy-low information.

WHAT I DID. Built scripts/omen_layer_probe.py -- the operator's falsification
test, run with NO node and NO fabric before any training run. Measures L0 vs
L1 vs L2 distinctness, then label_skew (does the coarse frame's LABEL
distribution skew), then a held-out arm: fit the motif->trough map on the
train window, freeze it, score the held-out window on per-trade net and
trough precision. Exits nonzero when a layer fails to abstract, so it gates.

RESULT 1 -- ABSTRACTION: YES. L0 mean of the 5 input streams 0.5441, L1
0.0139, a factor of 39. L1 is NOT cut.

RESULT 2 -- THE DILUTION FLOOR IS THE WRONG TEST FOR A LAYER. MIN_QUERY_
DISTINCTNESS is 0.20 and L1 reads 0.0139, so the law would auto-cut every
abstraction layer before it was measured. The law was measured on SENSORY
streams where low distinctness means constant means uninformative; a motif
layer is low-distinctness BY DESIGN. Use label skew instead.

RESULT 3 -- HELD-OUT EDGE: NEGATIVE, BOTH WINDOWS. In-sample lift is strong
(2.69x trough UP, 2.25x DOWN, sign agreeing across both). Held out it
collapses: per-trade net vs buy-every-bar -0.5901% UP (12 trades, unrankable)
and -0.2128% DOWN (109 trades). Trough precision 0.0% vs 7.1% UP, 17.4% vs
14.3% DOWN. A 2.25-2.69x in-sample lift becoming a +3.1pp precision bump with
a negative net is a map fitted to the train window's regime.

RESULT 4 -- THE SELL-HIGH HALF HAD NEVER BEEN SCORED. omen_experiment.py:552
is long-only so a crest is an abstention. Scored crest against forward returns
(not by shorting): fall precision 89.3% vs 73.8% base in DOWN, 23.6% vs 28.0%
in UP. ASYMMETRIC, so no edge claimed -- but the exit side is more informative
than the entry side on the same motifs, and nobody has been measuring it.

RESULT 5 -- THE ENCODER WAS BLIND, found by Gale's per-stream census and fixed
here. _band_of counted only u/d/r prefixes; geometry frames are all q buckets,
so it never SAW the token and geometry read mid on 600/600 bars. Two live
slots of five. Fixed q banding: L1 vocabulary 10 -> 21/25 motifs. The held-out
edge did NOT improve (-0.9346% UP, -0.2128% DOWN unchanged).

RESULT 6 -- THE FIX BROKE L2's GUARD, and the sweep fixed it. A 4-step path
went 0.2017 -> 0.4520, over the 0.30 identifier guard. Swept: 2 -> 0.1266/
0.1530, 3 -> 0.2976/0.2962, 4 -> 0.4520/0.4159. Set to 3, margin 0.8%, thin
and flagged as thin.

NEXT: do NOT run an L0-vs-L0+L1 node arm on this corpus -- the stream does not
carry held-out buy-low signal, and there is no pool 20 in any identity toml
anyway. Two things are worth a pass: (1) volatility still saturates at hi on
~100% of bars (three u tokens every bar by construction) -- band each stream
against ITS OWN distribution, Gale's suggestion; (2) the EXIT side, which is
measured nowhere and looked better than the entry side here.

FALSIFIED, and the premise was wrong rather than the threshold. WINDOW_SEC is 604800.0 -- the gate already reads the SAME seven days the census read. There is no window disagreement. The entire difference is MAX_TICK_GAP_SEC: the census counted consecutive ROWS, the gate counts rows adjacent IN TIME.

RESULT, one 7d window, >5% jumps split by the gap they span:
  BASECAT-USDC  1809 pairs  p99 5.272% by row / 2.646% at <=120s  23 jumps >5%, ZERO within 120s (min gap 281s, median 2135s), largest move inside 120s all week 4.472%

  AERO-USDC     3668 pairs  p99 0.862% by row / 0.426% at <=120s   1 jump >5%, spanning 22 hours

So BASECAT's admission is CORRECT and closes with no change to the gate's logic. The 120s measure is the right one: a stop is only enforceable on a tick that ARRIVES, so a 5% move accumulated across 35 minutes of feed silence is not a move the stop failed to bind on. It is load-bearing rather than cosmetic -- it separates the symbol that booked six 17-25% gross ghost rows from the one that booked a single row, and row-adjacent p99 does not separate them.

## 2026-09-11 — Iris (pass 119) — stale_exit_secs now runs on a wall clock

**Hypothesis:** `stale_exit_secs` (900s) is a wall-clock promise enforced on a
tick-driven schedule, so the positions that most need rule 4 are the ones least
able to reach it. Pass 102 fixed the elif ORDER (1cc2a6a) and rule 4 can now
fire, but it still needs a tick on the held symbol — and `_handle_sample` gates
that tick behind the model-window check and the duplicate-signature return.

**RESULT: CONFIRMED and fixed.** `TradingBot._close_stale_positions_on_the_clock`
runs the EXISTING exit chain with a NEUTRAL model read (so only the position's
own target, stop and clock can close it) on ANY symbol's tick, beside the
dark-feed sweeps and ABOVE them — a mark fresh enough to book honestly should
close and record an outcome; only one too dark to mark out should be abandoned
recording nothing. Bounded: marks older than 900s refused (the +161% stale
repricing), live positions untouched (they have `_exit_dark_live_positions`), one
in-flight claim per `symbol:trade_id` so two bots cannot double-book one round
trip, and one `_stale_exit_secs()` read shared with the chain.

**THE NUMBER, `scripts/hold_time_edge.py --days 14`, n=74 timed trips:** median
hold 58.8 → 15.5 min; share outliving clock+30s 86% → 4%; 62 of 74 swept. That
is a labelled REPLAY counterfactual against the ticks each trip actually
received, not a post-fix book — production must be restarted for the real one.
The threshold carries the sweep's 30s period on both columns: against a bare 900s
every swept trip still reads as outliving the clock and the share printed 86%
before and 86% after while the median fell by 43 minutes.

**NOT CLAIMED:** the ≤15 min bucket is still n=10, under this loop's n≥30 floor,
so it is not ranked and no edge is claimed. The split is over REALISED trips, so
a trip may have closed fast BECAUSE it hit its target; this moves the population
so the question can be asked at n≥30. **NEXT:** restart production, then price
the post-fix ≤15 min bucket per-trade against buy-every-bar in an UP and a DOWN
window. Report: docs/STALE_EXIT_WALL_CLOCK.md. 8 new tests, 37 green in the
related exit-chain files.

2026-09-16 Echo (senior, pass 424, third entry) -- SYNTHESIS OF TWO AGENTS' NUMBERS, and the clip finding that came out of it.

Sage solved the fee model exactly from trade_fills.details this pass: ROUND TRIP = 0.003862*notional + 0.0041 dollars. The 0.0041 is FIXED gas, so percentage cost collapses with clip size: 0.933% at a 0.75 clip, 0.591% at 2.00, 0.468% at 5, 0.427% at 10, 0.404% at the 23.18 wallet, 0.386% at an infinite clip. Crossed against my 72h move table (p90 absolute move over a 15-40 min window), the MINIMUM CLIP each symbol needs before its p90 move pays for the round trip: ZORA 1.032% pays at every clip including 0.75; CAKE 0.981% from ~0.70; OP 0.773% needs ~1.10; LINK 0.559% needs ~2.40; WBTC 0.523% needs ~3.00; AERO 0.416% needs ~13.80; WETH-USDC 0.246% NEVER pays -- it is below the 0.386% infinite-clip floor at any size.

THREE RESULTS. (1) THE 0.75 CLIP IS ITSELF A BINDING CONSTRAINT, not just the signal: at 0.75 only ZORA and CAKE ever clear, at 23.18 six symbols clear on p90. The fixed gas term makes a small clip a percentage tax, and this loop has been grading signal quality at the one clip where almost nothing can pay. This REFINES the older 'a bigger clip is arithmetically dead' note, which was computed against a pure-rate model with no fixed term -- with the fixed term the clip buys 0.933% -> 0.404%, a 2.3x improvement, bounded below by 0.386%. (2) 'RESTRICT TO DEEP POOLS' IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY RIGHT: WETH is the cheapest token to swap and the quietest, p90 0.246% under a 0.386% floor. The correct ranking axis is MOVE MINUS COST per symbol, not cost alone.

(3) THE CAVEAT THAT GOVERNS ALL OF IT, recorded so nobody quotes the table without it: the 0.3862% variable rate is solved from OUR book, which is dominated by AERO-class tokens, while the operator's direct quotes put WETH at 0.04-0.11% -- about a tenth of it. So that rate is a BLEND over the traded mix, not a per-symbol truth, and every row above inherits the blend. If WETH's true variable rate is ~0.1%, its floor at a 23 clip is ~0.118% and its 0.246% p90 move DOES pay, which inverts result (2) completely. UNRESOLVED AND NOW THE HIGHEST-VALUE UNKNOWN IN THE REPO: the PER-SYMBOL variable rate. That is what [984354f7] and [bc7b37c2] exist to obtain, and it is why ZORA -- the best-fed high-movement symbol we have, 1251 ticks at a 13s gap -- must be cost-quoted first.

## PASS 428 -- Echo (senior). THE SELECTION BAR IS 5-12bp, AND IT IS THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE RESULT

**Route:** brute-force the predicate space instead of screening hand-written
strategies, with the best-of-N null computed INSIDE the search.
**Tool:** `scripts/predicate_forge.py` (b4e018f). One command:
`python -X utf8 scripts/predicate_forge.py --hours 168 --perms 120 --fee 0.00055`

### Why this is not another strategy screen

Every prior screen here tested rules a human wrote down. This enumerates:
34 features x 6 quantile cuts x 2 directions = **408 predicates**, priced at
2/3/5/8/12 min over 32,336 ticks and 155 symbols. Three families never covered
before: derivatives ABOVE the first (acceleration, jerk), volatility ratio as
an axis independent of direction, and the cross-sectional state at each instant
(crowd mean, dispersion, this symbol's rank within it, residual after the crowd
is subtracted).

### THE NUMBER TO CARRY FORWARD

Forward returns permuted WITHIN symbol, the entire 408-predicate screen re-run
on the shuffled labels, 120 draws. This is the best lift reachable by selection
alone on this tape:

```
  horizon    bar median    bar 95th pct
    2 min       5.55bp         8.42bp
    3 min       5.40bp         7.91bp
    5 min       5.83bp         8.48bp
    8 min       6.81bp         9.65bp
   12 min       8.30bp        11.59bp
```

**Any single-predicate lift under ~9bp on this tape is indistinguishable from
noise, and at 12 min the bar is 11.59bp.** This retroactively explains the
graveyard: b702171 led with donchian_breakout at +15.32bp in-sample -- 1.3x the
12-min bar -- and inverted out of sample, exactly as an order statistic should.

### The result: the single-predicate space is EMPTY out of sample

159 of 408 predicates cleared the bar IN-SAMPLE across the five horizons.
**Exactly ONE held out of sample** (same sign, still over the bar):

```
  xs_rank<q0.05  @ 2 min   IS +12.82bp (n=619)   OOS +9.31bp (n=443)
                           net at an 11bp WETH round trip:  -2.34bp
```

At 3/5/8/12 min, **zero** held. The price-action families (return, acceleration,
jerk, vol ratio, range position) post +17 to +28bp in sample and collapse to
about 0bp out of sample at every horizon. That IS the selection effect, made
visible for the first time in this repo.

`r3>q0.95` shows net +0.47bp at 2 min and +1.50bp at 3 min but its sign FLIPS
between splits (-11.89 IS / +12.13 OOS). That is a coin landing twice, not a
signal. Do not resurrect it without a third window.

### CLOSED and NOT CLOSED

**CLOSED:** single-predicate price-action search at 2-12 min on the pooled
universe. Independently confirms `price-action-predicates-are-exhausted` by a
different method, and now with a bar attached.

**NOT CLOSED, and this is the lead:** the cross-sectional family is the only one
that kept its sign AND magnitude out of sample. `xs_rank<q0.05` -- "this symbol
is the worst performer in the market at this instant" -- reverts. It misses the
cheapest round trip on base by 2.34bp, which is the smallest gap any route here
has posted. It was also never tuned: 2 min was the shortest horizon screened and
q0.05 the most extreme cut offered. Both are corners of the grid, so the true
optimum may lie outside it.

**NOT TESTED:** conjunctions. Every predicate here is a single term. The forge
prices one feature at a time; 408 choose 2 is ~83k pairs, and the selection bar
rises with the candidate count -- which the forge already knows how to measure.

### The methodological rule this pass earns

**No screen in this repo should report a lift again without reporting the bar
it had to clear.** A lift without its selection bar is not a measurement. The
forge computes the bar for any predicate set handed to it; use it.

`python -X utf8 scripts/xs_rank_depth_check.py --cut 0.05 --horizon 5`

The +10.73bp was priced at a flat 11bp round trip, which is a promise about
POOL DEPTH. Split the 510 held-out fires by the depth snapshot (28d3db1):

```
  bucket              fires   share   gross bp  round trip    NET bp

  mid  $250k-1M           1   0.2%    +163.43        128bp    +35.43   <- n=1, ignore
  thin $50k-250k         33   6.5%     +15.77        400bp   -384.23
  dust  <$50k            22   4.3%      +4.22       1500bp  -1495.78
  NOT IN SNAPSHOT       397  77.8%      +9.18     unknown       n/a
```

**ON THE POOLS WE CAN ACTUALLY FILL, THE LIFT IS +0.88bp, NOT +10.73bp.** The
aggregate number was carried by the thin bucket (+15.77bp at a 400bp cost) and
by the 77.8% whose depth is unknown and which are more likely thin than deep.
The single mid-bucket row at +163bp is n=1 and must not be quoted.

**ROUTE CLOSED.** Cross-sectional reversion is real -- it beat its selection bar
by 2-3x with a monotone dose-response across eight ladders, and that part
replicates -- but its skill lives in pools whose round trip eats it 20x over.
This is the THIRD independent arrival at the same wall
(`ghost-book-profit-is-in-untradeable-pools`, `dip-supply-is-in-the-thin-tokens`,
and now this), by three unrelated methods.

**THE LAW THIS ESTABLISHES, and the next pass should treat it as a screen, not a
discovery:** on this venue, predictability and fillability are ANTI-CORRELATED.
Thin pools move predictably BECAUSE they are thin -- few participants, so one
flow dominates the next print -- and that same thinness is what makes the round
trip 400-1500bp. Any future screen that pools the universe will keep rediscovering
this and keep being wrong. **Screen on the deep subset from the start.** On deep
pools the honest number for the best predicate found by a 408-wide enumerated
search is +0.88bp against a 22bp round trip.

**2. THE GRADUATION BAR CANNOT RESOLVE ANY EDGE WE COULD EARN. This is the

The win-rate leg is exact: 55% of 20 is 11/20, which a p=0.5 coin clears

**Only 30.8% of our 227 book rows sit in the tier where anything is provable.**
Filed as [ceadb8da].

## Pass 432 (Echo, senior) -- the download-worker deadline, and pricing the operator's brute-force request

ROUTE TRIED: bound the wedged download worker so `data_ingest` stops being
stranded behind it. STATUS: code shipped, NOT yet measured in production.

Commit 64744c9. `TokenDownloadSupervisor._run_worker` now runs each worker on its
own daemon thread and joins with WORKER_DEADLINE_SEC (default 300, env
DOWNLOAD_SUPERVISOR_WORKER_DEADLINE_SEC). Past the deadline the cycle walks away
and the workers after it -- including `market`, which writes the prices table --
still get their turn. The abandoned thread is remembered per label and that label
is SKIPPED while it is alive, so at most ONE thread per worker is ever
outstanding; the skip lifts by itself when the call returns. Checked the two ways
this could have been wrong: db.py:78 builds ONE sqlite connection with
check_same_thread=False behind a lock, so running workers on fresh threads has no
thread-affinity problem and leaks no per-thread connection.

the box stays full. We go dark and nothing is fixed. Ineffectiveness, not
unfairness -- and that is the same mechanism as the 57.6h darkness.

the memory term in both should_pause and should_throttle. It returns False --
old behaviour, full force -- in the three cases where shedding still works:
no sample yet (unknown is not exhausted), free memory under _MIN_FREE_MB (256)
where the next allocation fails whoever caused it, and our own tree at >=75% of
its RSS budget where the memory genuinely IS ours. CPU is untouched: a busy CPU
is real contention whoever owns the processes.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, AND NOBODY SHOULD CLAIM IT:

  * 18 -> 40 is the LIMIT FUNCTION, not realised evidence. Pair breadth is not
    evidence rate one-for-one and the conversion is unmeasured.

### Pass 437 addendum -- does pair BREADTH predict entries? Yes, and it beats tick volume

The 18 -> 40 figure above is the limit function, not evidence, so it needed an
independent reason to matter. 36 hourly buckets, market_stream vs trading_ops
(action='enter'):

    RAW, all 36 buckets     corr(symbols, enter) = +0.802
                            above-mean breadth  25.7 enter/h
                            below-mean breadth   8.0 enter/h

NOT POSTED AS-IS, because blackouts zero BOTH terms: a dead hour has 0 symbols
and 0 entries, which manufactures correlation out of uptime alone. Dropping the
11 dead hours, keeping the 25 hours the feed was live:

    corr(SYMBOLS, enter) = +0.540    <- breadth
    corr(TICKS,   enter) = +0.379    <- raw tick volume
    corr(SYMBOLS, TICKS) = +0.036    <- collinearity

The effect survives the control at ~2/3 its raw size. At n=25 the 5% critical r
is ~0.396: breadth clears it (t=3.08, p~0.005); raw tick volume does NOT
(t=1.96, p~0.06). And breadth and tick volume are ORTHOGONAL at +0.036 -- they
are not two views of the same quantity, and the one that predicts entries is
BREADTH, which is exactly what the governor was clamping from 40 to 18.

NOT PROVEN, and nobody should promote it: observational. Breadth varied over
those 36 hours for uncontrolled reasons, entry ops are not settled trades, and
a cross-hour correlation is not proof that raising the cap raises entries. The
causal test is the restart, filed as [7a1b8684] p1.

METHOD NOTE, the reusable part: when both the cause and the effect go to zero
during an outage, ANY correlation between them is partly uptime. Drop the dead
buckets before quoting the number. +0.802 became +0.540 here, and the raw
figure would have been the third "too good" number this repo shipped.

### Pass 437 CORRECTION -- the +0.540 above is 96.8% CANDIDATES. Do not use it.

The breadth result two sections up controlled for uptime and then failed to
check what the dependent variable WAS. `action='enter'` in trading_ops breaks
down, last 48h, as:

    316  ghost_candidate
    255  ghost_candidate_quote_ok
     19  ghost-entry

So 96.8% of the series I correlated against symbol breadth were CANDIDATES.
"More symbols streamed produce more candidate rows on those symbols" is close
to mechanical, and +0.540 is not evidence that breadth produces entries.

CLOSED: "breadth predicts entry production, therefore the governor clamp was
costing entries." Not established. The breadth -> ENTRY link CANNOT be measured
at this rate: 19 real ghost-entries in 48h, and only 8 of 36 hours contain even
one. A series that is zero 78% of the time does not support an hourly
correlation and none should be manufactured.

WHAT THE BREAKDOWN DOES ESTABLISH, and it is worth more than the error:
CANDIDATE SUPPLY IS NOT THE BOTTLENECK. 571 candidates / 48h (~286/day) convert
to 19 entries -- 3.3% -- and quote_ok -> entry is 19/255 = 7.5%. Candidates are
produced in bulk and almost none become entries. The lever is CONVERSION, not
supply, which agrees with the ghost-route finding already on record.

THIS TEMPERS THE GOVERNOR FIX AND THAT IS STATED DELIBERATELY: raising the pair
cap 18 -> 40 raises candidate supply. At 3.3% conversion, more supply buys
proportionally little. The fix is still correct -- shedding our own work on
other programs' memory is a defect regardless, and the 18 vs 40 clamp is
measured fact -- but its expected PAYOFF was oversold here, and [7a1b8684]
should be read as "measure whether this helps", not "this will help".

METHOD NOTE, and this repo keeps paying for it: controlling for the confound you
thought of is not the same as knowing what your dependent variable is. Break the
outcome series down by status BEFORE correlating anything against it.

THE GENERALISING CLAIM: this backlog is not 107 pieces of work. It is roughly 25
defects filed four or five times each, because each pass re-derives the same
finding from the same data and files it fresh. Filing reads as output; searching
does not. The consequence is that an agent handed "the top p1 item" is usually
handed a duplicate rather than the most important thing, and that a single fix
is split across ids so no one of them is ever finishable.

THE RULE: before scrum.py add, grep scrum.py list for the function or file you
are about to name. If it is there, refine it with scrum.py accept. Rejecting a
duplicate does not touch the throughput number, so nothing is lost by collapsing
one.

### Pass 445 SELF-CORRECTION: my own harness ran a 4x TIGHTER RULE THAN PRODUCTION

THE BUG, and it is a one-line import. `os.getenv("MONEY_BUTTON_MIN_DRAWDOWN",

dotenv first. Importing anything under services/ does that as a side effect.
scripts/money_button_dip_expectancy.py imports services.round_trip_cost and so
gets the SHIPPED value; my scripts/clip_size_expectancy.py imported only numpy
and sqlite3 and so got the literal.

    BEFORE any repo import:  MONEY_BUTTON_MIN_DRAWDOWN = None
    AFTER  services.round_trip_cost:  '0.005'

harnesses printed different bands for the same rule -- mine "[-5%, -2%]", the

goes 99 -> 330. The rule's admission test (expected_return - fee >= min_net) is
doing double duty as a QUALITY FILTER -- the expensive version trades less and
better, the cheap version trades more and worse, and the two effects cancel
almost exactly. **The dip rule's edge and its cost are locked together.**

CONSEQUENCE, AND IT CLOSES THE ROUTE PROPERLY. money_button's dip does not
fail on cost, and it does not fail on signal. It fails on BOTH JOINTLY: there
is no cost level at which it pays significantly, because lowering the cost
lowers the bar. The +0.1769% at t=+3.45 is real but it belongs to a
99-trade high-quality subset that the 31.5bp floor sits above, and you cannot
keep that subset while paying less for it -- the subset IS defined by what you
pay.

[017594f6] IS NOT WITHDRAWN but its upside is now MEASURED AND BOUNDED: the
best it can do for money_button is +4bp at t=+1.07. It remains worth doing for
a different reason -- roundtrip_cost_rate is wired in as an ENTRY GATE
([84e62c6d]) and a 2.5x-too-high slippage figure there refuses trades on every
rule, not just this one. Do NOT take the item expecting it to make
money_button pay. It will not.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE for a dip route to work: an admission test that
does NOT contain the fee, so selectivity can be tuned independently of cost.
That is a rule-shape change, not a cost fix, and nobody has costed it.

### Pass 445 FINAL: the rule-shape escape hatch is closed too -- expected_return does not predict realised

I ended the postscript above saying "what would have to be true is an admission
test that does NOT contain the fee, so selectivity can be tuned independently
of cost -- and nobody has costed it." I had time, so I costed it.

Admit on `expected_return >= BAR` with fee=0 (so selectivity is INDEPENDENT of
cost), then charge the real 0.3606% at settlement. Deep universe, $10, 5m:

        bar     n  per day   mean gross    mean net       t
      0.50%   429    19.95     +0.0981%    -0.2625%   -8.23
      0.75%   199     9.26     +0.0920%    -0.2686%   -4.76
      1.00%   115     5.35     +0.0905%    -0.2701%   -2.95
      1.50%    37     1.72     +0.2394%    -0.1212%   -1.21
      2.00%     9     0.42     +0.0647%    -0.2959%   -0.90
      3.00%     0       --           --          --      --

**GROSS IS FLAT AT ~0.09% ACROSS A 2x RANGE OF THE BAR, AND NEVER REACHES THE
0.3149% FLOOR.** Demanding twice the expected move (0.5% -> 1.0%) leaves
realised gross unchanged at +0.09% while n drops 429 -> 115. The 1.5% row at
+0.2394% is n=37 and t=-1.21 -- not a signal, and 2.0% falls straight back to
+0.0647%.

THE CONCLUSION, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE NEGATIVE: **the rule's own
`expected_return` estimate carries essentially no information about the trade's
realised return.** A selectivity knob cannot be built, because the quantity it
would select on is uninformative. The rule-shape fix does not exist.

ONE HONEST NOTE ON WHY THIS GROSS (+0.09%) IS LOWER THAN THE +0.1769% I
reported for the fee-coupled version at n=99: the fee also enters the TARGET
(`tp = max(fee + min_net, |dd| * rev_frac)`), so a real fee sets a HIGHER
take-profit and the trades that touch it book more. That +0.1769% is therefore
a TARGET-HEIGHT effect, not better selection -- which is consistent with
everything above and makes the finding tighter, not weaker.

ROUTE STATUS: the money_button dip on deep pools is now closed on all three
axes -- supply (2.37 candidates/day), cost (no level pays, t=+1.07 at zero
slippage), and shape (expected_return does not predict). It should not be
reopened without a NEW predicate, not a new threshold.

entire burst. A 110-row swing in twenty minutes is what that looks like.

WHY REALISED SLIPPAGE IS THE WHOLE COST, not a part of it. services/fill_cost.py
:30-38, written by an earlier pass, states it outright: an AMM takes its fee out
of the output amount, so the DEX fee is NOT separately measurable and arrives
already inside executed_price. Realised slippage is therefore "the whole
economic cost of the fee plus spread plus impact together". Round trip =
slippage + gas, both measured.

THE NUMBER. Deep tokens only (AERO, CBBTC, CBETH), legs adverse-signed (entry
+slip, exit -slip), one decimals-artifact row censored -- CBETH-USDC live_entry
expected 2731.12 executed 2.739721e-09, a 1e12 factor, the known decimals bug.

"ten rows set the book's sign" trap.

    slippage   29 legs   6.7bp/leg   ROUND TRIP 13.4bp   sd 26.8  95pct CI [-6,+34]
    gas        38 legs   median 0.00000093 ETH/leg, MEASURED from receipts

        clip  $3  ->  32-41 bp      <- what we actually traded, every time
        clip $10  ->  19-22 bp
        clip $23  ->  16-17 bp      <- the whole deployable wallet

    Production charges a symbol-blind 42.5bp at EVERY clip.

THE MECHANISM, trading/pipeline.py:6268:
    recommended_live_usd = recommended_ratio * deployable_stable
with recommended_ratio ~0.047-0.107, so a $23 wallet yields a $1.10-2.47 clip.
The absolute caps (LIVE_MAX_BOOTSTRAP_USD=150, LIVE_FIRST_TRANCHE_USD=50, at
pipeline.py:6261-6262) sit far above the wallet and NEVER BIND. The binding
constraint is the percentage ratio. Percentage-of-capital sizing is right for a
large account and INVERTED for a small one, because gas is fixed per
transaction, not proportional: the ratio protects against a loss smaller than
the fee it forces the trade to pay.

WHY IT IS AN EDGE. h* = 0.5 + cost/(2*mean_abs_move), WETH mean_abs_move

### Pass 454 addendum -- the stall has a FEEDBACK LOOP, and it is pinned at the cap

Kept measuring after filing [3de9a523]. Two refinements, both from the same log
tail, and one correction to myself.

THE SELF-THROTTLE. 932 warnings of "market-stream: consensus failure throttling
REST polls". Latest state per symbol:

  84 symbols throttled
  backoff ladder observed: 1.6 -> 2.6 -> 4.1 -> 6.6 -> 10.5 -> 16.8 -> 26.8
                           -> 42.9 -> 68.7 -> 110 -> 120s  (~1.6x, capped 120)
  640 of 936 throttle events sit at the 120.0s CAP
  worst: GROVE-USDC 356 failures, TRADE-USDC 348, STONKLESS-USDC 348,
         FLOW-USDC 348, HONTER-USDC 336, ARB-USDC 292

This closes the loop on the stall. The loop stalls -> in-flight REST calls time
out -> timeouts count as CONSENSUS failures -> _grow_rest_interval fires every
4th failure (data_stream.py:1754) -> the symbol ratchets to the 120s cap. The
feed then polls slower, which is indistinguishable from a dead upstream.

NOTE THE INCOMPLETE FIX. :3674 deliberately does NOT charge the ENDPOINT when
it can see our own loop was blocked -- someone already understood this failure.
But the per-symbol CONSENSUS counter still increments, so the endpoint's
reputation is protected and the symbol's poll interval is not. That is the gap.

CORRECTION TO MYSELF: I first read the greps as "there is no shrink path, the
interval is a one-way ratchet". WRONG -- _relax_rest_interval exists at :3064
and :3227 decrements the failure counter on success. The defect is not absence,
it is ASYMMETRY: grow is one step per 4 failures, recovery is one decrement per
success, and with the loop blocked 88% of the time successes are scarce.
GROVE-USDC at 356 failures needs 356 clean polls at a 120s interval -- 11.9h of
uninterrupted success -- to unwind. It will not get it while the loop stalls.

WHAT THE 84 SYMBOLS ARE. GROVE, TRADE, STONKLESS, HONTER, AICAT,
USELESSLAPTOP, $GTRADE, "ONLINE, ONCHAIN, ONBASE", DIDDYOIL, CLAWDCHAT. Junk
microcaps we will never trade, each consuming poll budget and executor threads
on a 6-CPU box shared with ~30 streams. Consistent with the known 39.3%
untradeable-pair contamination.

FOURTH SUSPECT FOR THE STALL ITSELF, and I now rank it above the DNS pool.
Executor starvation makes requests TIME OUT; it cannot make the loop thread
miss 2230 seconds. Only work on the loop thread, or CPU/GIL starvation of the
whole process, does that. Measured: production worker PID 32632 has burned
90005 CPU-seconds in 74880 wall-seconds -- 1.20 cores sustained for 20.8h --
inside ONE GIL with 57 threads, on a 6-CPU box at 74.9% RAM. A loop thread
competing with 56 others for the GIL against 1.2 cores of continuous burn is a
mechanism that fits the observed lag magnitude. Not proven. Measure it before
fixing it.

### Pass 454 -- CAUSE FOUND AND PROVEN BY DIRECT SAMPLING. 4 of 4 samples, same frame.

Stopped guessing and sampled the loop thread. .venv/Scripts/py-spy.exe, read-only,
PID 32632 (the real production worker -- NOT 22664). Four independent dumps, and
the event-loop thread was in the SAME frame every time:

    _handle_sample            trading/bot.py:6175      <- PER-TICK handler, on the loop
      _maybe_transition_to_live  trading/bot.py:4560
        _ghost_validation_for_live trading/pipeline.py:4702
          _ghost_validation        trading/pipeline.py:4761
            ghost_trade_snapshot   trading/metrics.py:387
              fetch_trades         db.py:1846
                _cursor            db.py:654           <- BLOCKING sqlite, on the loop

A SYNCHRONOUS SQLITE QUERY AGAINST THE 25.9 GB STORE (1.66 GB WAL, synchronous=
FULL) IS RUNNING DIRECTLY ON THE ASYNCIO EVENT LOOP, INSIDE THE PER-TICK SAMPLE
HANDLER. Not in an executor. Not awaited. On the loop.

A SECOND blocking DB path is on the same loop in every sample:
    record_metrics db.py:1660 -> _maybe_prune_metrics db.py:1688 -> _cursor db.py:654

WHY THIS IS THE ANSWER AND NOT ANOTHER SUSPECT:
  - it is ON THE LOOP THREAD, so it produces loop_lag. Executor/DNS starvation
    (my suspect c) cannot -- it makes requests time out without lagging the loop.
    Suspect (c) is now CLOSED as a cause of the lag.
  - it DOES NOT LOG, which is exactly what my 384-stall elimination predicted.
  - py-spy marks the thread "idle", i.e. blocked on I/O, not burning CPU. So
    GIL/CPU starvation (my suspect a, which I had ranked FIRST) is WRONG as the
    mechanism. I had the right shortlist and the wrong order; the 90005 CPU-s on
    32632 is real but is not what stalls the loop.
  - the 1.66 GB WAL (suspect b) is not the cause but is the AMPLIFIER: it is what
    makes each fetch_trades slow enough to stall the loop for minutes.

THREE SYMPTOMS, ONE CAUSE -- which is what the standing instructions predicted:
  step 1  FEED   "no ticks in 10min"      -> the loop running the market streams
                                             is blocked by this query
  step 6  RISK   "ghost_validation_block" -> the SAME _ghost_validation call
  step 10 PROFIT 0 fills / 0 outcomes 20.8h -> nothing executes on a stalled loop

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX (for exec, not decided here): get fetch_trades off the loop
and stop calling it per tick. It is a ghost-evidence aggregate feeding a
transition decision -- it does not need to be recomputed on every sample, and it
must not be recomputed synchronously on the loop. Cache it with a TTL, or move
it to a worker. Checkpointing the WAL will make it faster and will NOT fix it.

REPRODUCE: .venv/Scripts/py-spy.exe dump --pid <production pid>  -- grep for
fetch_trades and run_forever in the same thread block.

  -- Echo

### Pass 454 -- THE MECHANISM, MEASURED, AND THE FIX IS ONE LINE

fetch_trades (db.py:1846) ends in:  FROM trading_ops {clause} ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT ?
trading_ops has 95555 rows and TWO indexes: (wallet, ts) and (status, ts).
NEITHER can serve a bare ORDER BY ts. Measured, read-only, on the live store:

  EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN  select * from trading_ops ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 500
      SCAN trading_ops
      USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY
  TIMED cold: 29.00 s      TIMED warm: 3.14 s      (500 rows)

COUNTERFACTUAL, same table, same limit, a clause that CAN use an existing index:
  EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN  ... where wallet=? ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 500
      SEARCH trading_ops USING INDEX idx_trading_ops_wallet_ts (wallet=?)
  TIMED: 0.004 s

7250x cold, 785x warm. The only difference is whether an index serves the sort.

THIS CLOSES THE MAGNITUDE QUESTION. A 29-second query running per tick on the
event loop, under write contention against a 1.66 GB WAL, sits squarely inside
the measured stall distribution (p50 54s, p90 177s). The numbers agree from two
independent directions -- log-derived lag counters, and a direct timing of the
query the py-spy dump caught the loop inside.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE:
    CREATE INDEX idx_trading_ops_ts ON trading_ops(ts);
It is additive, changes no behaviour, and turns 29 s into ~4 ms.

DO BOTH ANYWAY. The index removes the 29 s. Getting fetch_trades off the loop
and out of the per-tick path removes the CLASS of bug -- any future unindexed
predicate on that path stalls the feed again. The index is the emergency stop;
the executor/TTL move is the fix. An index alone, shipped alone, will look like
a cure and leave the loop one bad query away from this same 20.8h of silence.

CAUTION FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE INDEX: this is a 25.9 GB store with a 1.66 GB WAL
and a live writer. CREATE INDEX takes a write lock and will itself block
production while it builds. Do it against a stopped production, or accept a
stall while it runs, and checkpoint the WAL first. Measure the build.

  -- Echo

### Pass 454 close -- I TIMED THE FIX ON A COPY, AND MY OWN CAUTION WAS OVERSTATED

I warned above that CREATE INDEX would take a write lock on a 25.9 GB store and
block production while it built, and told whoever takes it to stop production
first. I then measured it instead of leaving that as a warning, because an
unquantified caution is how a one-line fix sits in a backlog for a week.

Copied trading_ops (95555 rows, 321 MB) to a scratch db and built the index:

    CREATE INDEX idx_trading_ops_ts ON trading_ops(ts)     ->  0.26 s
    EXPLAIN after:  SCAN trading_ops USING INDEX idx_trading_ops_ts
    TIMED after:    0.0029 s      (was 29.00 s cold)

0.26 s, not minutes. busy_timeout is 5000 ms, so concurrent writers WAIT rather
than fail for the whole build window. RETRACT MY OWN CAUTION: production does
not need stopping for this. It is a sub-second lock and a DROP INDEX undoes it.

AND NOTE THIS -- NO RESTART IS NEEDED. An index changes the query PLAN, not the
code. Production picks it up on the next fetch_trades call. This is the rare fix
in this repo that does not cost a 13-minute boot to test, which makes it the
cheapest thing on the entire backlog to verify.

Query speedup end to end: 29.00 s -> 0.0029 s, 10000x.

WHY I STILL DID NOT SHIP IT. This seat does not write production code, and a
one-line change I could "just do" is exactly the change the role says to hand
over. I also could not have watched it: I have minutes left, and the honest test
is loop-blocked%% over hours, not a green light at the moment of the write. It
is in [3de9a523] fully de-risked -- cause proven, mechanism measured, fix named,
build cost timed, rollback stated. Whoever takes it should be done in an hour.

WHAT I WOULD DO FIRST NEXT PASS: ship the index, confirm blocked%% falls from
87.9%, and ONLY THEN decide whether the per-tick fetch_trades call still needs
moving off the loop. The index may reveal a second blocking query behind it --

### Pass 454 -- HALVING MY OWN TRAP CLAIM. I checked the callers instead of the plans.

    ... FROM trade_fills ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?
and the schema is `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, i.e. the rowid. The
plan is a bare SCAN with NO TEMP B-TREE -- it walks the rowid index backwards,
which is free at any size. Indexing trade_fills(ts) would be harmless and
useless. The reader was written correctly.

fetch_trade_outcomes (db.py:1025) runs
    FROM trade_outcomes {where} ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT ?

wallet it is a genuine bare ORDER BY ts, and that table grows with every trade
we settle. The trap is real for this one.

    CREATE INDEX idx_trading_ops_ts    ON trading_ops(ts);      <- fixes today
    CREATE INDEX idx_trade_outcomes_ts ON trade_outcomes(ts);   <- fixes later

idle threads too, which is how `_cursor` showed on two background threads.

problem for two passes.

## Pass 456 -- the symbol-selection sort key is monotone in VARIANCE

**Route tried:** [ceadb8da] -- concentrate a rate-limited evidence budget on the
>$1M depth tier, because trades-to-resolve goes as sigma^2 and measured sigma is
97.3bp (n=70) in >$1M versus 590.5bp (n=72) one tier down. **Status: OPEN, with
the diagnosis finished and the implementation delegated.**

**CRITERION 1 IS PROVEN, three commands, all clean.**

    grep -rn pool_depth_snapshot --include=*.py trading/ services/ main.py router_wallet.py
      -> EXIT 1, ZERO HITS

`data/pool_depth_snapshot.json` has **no production consumer at all**. All 11 of
its references live under `scripts/`. It is measurement-only, which independently
re-confirms `pool-depth-snapshot-is-measurement-only`.

The path that actually spends the evidence budget:

    services/streamed_symbol_candidates.py:203
        found.sort(key=lambda c: c.clear_rate, reverse=True)

consumed by `services/atf_static_strategy.py:1471` (`_add_streamed_candidates`),
called at `:1680`. `atf_static*` takes 179 of ~186 decision cycles in 6h and holds
70% of all ghost evidence, so this **one sort line** spends most of the budget.
`grep -ci "depth|liquidity|tvl|reserve"` on that file returns **0** -- the word
depth does not appear in the file that decides what we look at.

**THE FINDING THAT MATTERS, and it is worse than the item described.**
`clear_rate` is defined at `:122` as the share of non-overlapping windows whose
**HIGH** cleared the round trip, measured from the window **OPEN**. That is a
volatility statistic and an upper bound on what a trade could have captured --
not what it would capture. Higher variance -> higher window high -> higher
clear_rate -> ranked first -> more decision cycles.

**The sort key is a monotone increasing function of the exact quantity that makes
evidence expensive.** We rank by a proxy for sigma, descending, and then wonder
why 69% of the budget lands where nothing is resolvable. This is not a missing
feature; it is a backwards one. The module's own docstring ranks AERO-WETH first
at 44.4% of windows, and AERO is the most-traded ghost symbol in the book.

**A THIRD TOKEN-BLIND COST CONSTANT, upstream of the two we knew about.**

    services/streamed_symbol_candidates.py:76
        ROUND_TRIP_COST = float(os.getenv("STREAMED_CANDIDATE_COST", "0.0065"))

One flat 65bp bar for every token, used as **both** the admission test and the
ranking bar. We already knew about `round_trip_cost` (measured, read by gates) and
`roundtrip_cost` (constant, read by entries). This one is upstream of both and
decides what we even look at. **Explicitly NOT claimed:** that this mis-charges by
6x-100x. The by-token cost spread is still UNMEASURED after two passes tried and
the quote-derived numbers were RETRACTED. The code fact is only that the bar is
identical for every token while measured per-token cost is not.

**SECOND FINDING, possibly larger, NOT yet proven.**

    services/atf_static_strategy.py:1490
        liquidity_usd=0.0,

Every streamed candidate is stamped with zero liquidity by hand, inside a block
whose comment says "Empty rather than invented". If any downstream gate tests
`liquidity_usd >= threshold`, every streamed candidate fails it **by
construction** -- not because the pool is thin but because nobody filled the field
in. That is a candidate explanation for backlog item `[23bb42fd]` ("the deep-pool
gate refuses 72 of 77 streamed symbols"). **I did not prove the gate reads this
field.** Treat it as a hypothesis. It also means re-ordering the offer list may be
necessary but insufficient, since a gate reading a hardcoded zero can undo the
ordering downstream.

**A THREAT TO THIS WHOLE ROUTE, recorded so the next pass does not miss it.**
The measured sigma is **NOT monotone in depth**: the $10k-$100k tier reads 82.6bp,
*lower* than the >$1M tier's 97.3bp. A strict 1/sigma^2 weighting would therefore
rank $10k-$100k FIRST and contradict the premise. The judgement made here was that
n=27 makes that estimate noisy and a monotone-in-depth weight is the defensible
choice -- but if that tier's sigma holds up as n grows, the depth proxy is wrong
and the route is dead. The item's own last criterion already says so.

**Not claimed, and must not be:** that deeper pools fill cheaper. `fb963cf`
falsified it -- AERO sits in a pool 4x deeper than CBBTC and costs 9x more to
round-trip at $2. Depth is used here as a proxy for VARIANCE only.

**Backlog hygiene.** `[6c361f13]` rejected as a duplicate of `[ceadb8da]` -- same
diagnosis, same fix, and two ids for one diagnosis orphans the evidence on

## Pass 458 -- Pike. SELECTION, NOT EXECUTION: the entries have no direction to eat.

**ROUTE.** The one question this loop had not asked: is the realised sub-coin-flip
hit rate a SELECTION failure (the entries carry no directional information) or an
EXECUTION failure (they carry information the exit rule destroys)? If the same
entries, scored at a FIXED horizon with the exit reason IGNORED, are directionally
positive, the edge exists and the exit is eating it -- and the whole problem moves.

**POPULATION, and it is 60% larger than the one everybody quotes.** `trading_ops`
`action='exit'`, deduped on `trade_id` (762 rows -> 431 distinct; the duplicates are
the re-drop artifact pass 105 recorded), keeping rows that carry `entry_ts` +
`entry_price` + `exit_price` with `entry_ts` inside the `market_stream` tape:
**n=376** (361 ghost-exit, 11 live-exit, 4 quarantined). `trade_outcomes` holds only
237. Both price legs read from `market_stream` so no denominator can mix sources;
returns as `(exit-entry)/entry`; `|r|>50%` censored.

**THE DESIGN POINT THAT DECIDES THE ANSWER -- a drifting tape hands you >0.5 for
free.** Raw entry-conditional forward returns look like a monster edge:

    fwd   5m  n=180  +9.43 bp     fwd  30m  n=233  +78.38 bp
    fwd  15m  n=187  +39.76 bp    fwd  60m  n=227 +116.88 bp   fwd 120m n=222 +96.44 bp

At 60 min a count-matched baseline of RANDOM ticks of the SAME symbol within +/-12 h
of each entry reads **+114.45 bp**. Entry minus baseline = **+0.84 bp, t=0.01**. The
entire +116.88 bp is unconditional drift on Base memecoins. **Any future pass that
reports a raw forward return without a drift-matched baseline will "find" a +117 bp
edge that is 99.3% tape drift.**

**THE PRIMARY TEST, distribution-free and immune to drift.** P(an entry's forward
return beats its OWN symbol's median forward return over +/-12 h). Under the null
this is **0.5000 exactly**, whatever the drift. Ties by midrank. Bar `sqrt(2 ln 10)`
= 2.146 (5 horizons x 2 statistics), stated before the look:

    H=  5m  n=180  beat 0.5194  CI[0.4468,0.5913]  z=+0.52
    H= 15m  n=187  beat 0.5401  CI[0.4686,0.6100]  z=+1.10
    H= 30m  n=233  beat 0.5215  CI[0.4575,0.5847]  z=+0.66
    H= 60m  n=227  beat 0.5198  CI[0.4550,0.5839]  z=+0.60
    H=120m  n=222  beat 0.5045  CI[0.4392,0.5696]  z=+0.13

**NOTHING CLEARS. Max |z| = 1.10. Every CI contains 0.5.** Robust to tie handling --
strict (tie=loss) / midrank / ties-dropped, all 15 variants inside the bar, max |z|
across all of them **1.11**, so the negative is not a tie artifact (I checked because
12.2% of 5-min forward returns are EXACTLY 0.0 and that would have biased it down).

**VERDICT: SELECTION. The exit rule is innocent -- there is no edge at entry to eat.**
A random tick of the same symbol in the same 24 h does as well as the bot's entry, at

fills — the file says so itself and says fills beat quotes where they disagree.

**The number.** Round-trip pool cost at a $2.00 clip, in bp, against the 38.6bp the flat gate
charges everything at a $6 clip:

**Why this is worse than "the constant is imprecise."** The gate is `if predicted <= rate:
reject`, so a HIGH rate refuses entries and a LOW rate admits them. The flat rate sits almost

it REFUSES the only three symbols we can fill cheaply and WAVES THROUGH the six that would eat
the account. It is not a precision problem, it is an inverted selector — the same shape already
recorded for `TOKEN_ROUND_TRIP`.

a DOLLAR PER LEG, so it is 1/clip. Carry the same dollars to a $20 clip and gas becomes 2.02bp:

    predicted all-in WETH round trip at $20 = 2.01 (pool) + 2.02 (gas) + SLIPPAGE_UNKNOWN ≈ 4bp + ?

The slippage term is the only unknown, and our 13.5bp constant is pooled over 38 legs containing

    clip       $0.75    $2.00    $6.00   $10.00

    VIRTUAL    31.7bp   67.6bp  180.9bp  291.6bp   INCREASING 9x (price impact dominates)

`roundtrip_cost_rate` is `FIXED/n + RATE` — **monotonically decreasing by construction**. One of

universe and 79% of ticks** on landing — a universe restriction wearing a cost fix's name.
Unpriced must return today's number **labelled and counted**, not refused.

**Status: the cost measurement is CLOSED. Coverage is OPEN and is now the binding constraint** —
a commit claiming "cost is per-symbol" is true for a fifth of the tape until `[15bce061]` runs.

### Pass 461 correction — MY "19.2x TOO STRICT" WAS WRONG. THE NUMBER IS 4.4x, AND A WORKER CAUGHT IT

Forge, building the per-symbol accessor, refused the census number I handed it and was right to.
**The census quotes POOL COST ONLY** — its own `THESE_ARE_QUOTES_NOT_FILLS.not_modelled` lists
*"gas (a dollar per leg, not a rate)"*. And `DEFAULT_FIXED_USD` 0.004047 **is** that gas: it
equals the census's own `measured_gas_context.median_round_trip_usd` to nine digits. So the
per-symbol rate is `FIXED/n + census_pool(symbol, n)` — the old formula with only the
token-blind *proportional* term replaced. Returning the raw census number would have **deleted
the gas charge from every symbol** (405bp at a $0.10 clip).

**My published ratio compared a $6 gate rate against a $2 pool-only cost.** Two errors stacked in
my favour: a clip mismatch and a missing gas term. Recomputed independently, apples-to-apples:

    clip $2   FLAT 52.10bp | WETH 22.24 (2.34x) | AERO 33.27 (1.57x) | VIRTUAL 87.85 (0.59x)
    clip $6   FLAT 38.62bp | WETH  8.79 (4.39x) | AERO 17.04 (2.27x) | VIRTUAL 187.62 (0.21x)

**The direction of every finding survives; the magnitudes do not.** WETH and AERO are still
over-charged and still the live cases. VIRTUAL is still under-charged and still the live
counterexample. But "19.2x too strict on WETH" is **4.4x**, and anyone who repeats 19.2x is
repeating my arithmetic error. The 1642x end-to-end spread across the full symbol set stands —
that one was computed within a single clip.

**The general trap, since this repo keeps stepping in it:** a cost that is `fixed + rate` cannot
be corrected by swapping in a number that measures only the rate. Check what a census excludes
before you treat it as a total. I read the file's own caveat block, quoted it approvingly on the
board, and then did exactly what it warned against.

**Route tried:** verify the pass-461 cost fix (`fe1f6e0`) by re-running it rather than reading the
report, then audit what it left behind. **Result: the fix is correct and the repo is now in a worse
state than before it landed.** Both halves of that sentence are measured.

**The fix holds.** `roundtrip_cost_rate` takes a symbol. At a $2 clip: WETH 22.24bp, AERO 33.27bp,
VIRTUAL 87.85bp, COMP 3321.77bp — they differ at one notional, and WETH < AERO < COMP. The
unchanged-but-labelled criterion was checked *against the old code* rather than asserted:
`git show HEAD~2:services/roundtrip_cost.py`, executed in isolation, returns 85.83 / 52.10 / 38.62bp
at $0.75 / $2 / $6, and the unpriced branch on HEAD returns 52.10 at $2. Byte-identical. No silent
universe restriction shipped. `SOURCE_CENSUS`, `SOURCE_UNPRICED`, `unpriced_symbols()` and
`_warn_unpriced` all exist, so unpriced is countable. Recorded with `scrum.py verify 84e62c6d` —
the first cross-verification on this board.

**What it left behind, and this is the finding.** `services/roundtrip_cost.py` and
`services/round_trip_cost.py` differ by one underscore, are both live, and now *both claim
per-symbol authority*. Round trip at a $2 clip, new vs old, bp:

| | roundtrip_cost | round_trip_cost | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| WETH | 22.24 | 11.00 | 0.5x |
| AERO | 33.27 | 435.00 | 13.1x |
| CBETH | 87.36 | 30.00 | 0.3x |
| KTA | 52.10 | 7498.00 | 143.9x |
| USDC | 52.10 | 11.00 | 0.2x |
| VIRTUAL | 87.85 | 70.00 | 0.8x |

**Before `fe1f6e0` these two could not be confused.** One was a flat curve of notional, the other a
per-token table — different shapes, so no reader mistook one for the other. They are now the same
shape, same units, same concept, and they contradict by up to 144x. Gates read `round_trip_cost`,
entries read `roundtrip_cost`, so an AERO round trip is plausibly admitted against 33bp and judged
against 435bp. **It is not a calibration offset**: the new module is cheaper on AERO and KTA and
*more expensive* on CBETH and USDC, so no single scale factor reconciles them. USDC — the quote side
of nearly every pair we trade — is unpriced in the new table and falls through to the 52.10bp
default while the old one calls it 11bp. Filed `[fa681912]`.

**NOT CLOSED, and deliberately so.** The complement is that the two modules count *different things*
(pool-only vs pool+gas, one leg vs two), making this a naming defect rather than a contradiction —
fix by renaming, not re-pricing. That must be settled before any number changes. This pass's own
`02f322f` is the cautionary case: Echo quoted a pool-only census figure as end-to-end and was wrong
by 4.4x. The item's first acceptance criterion is the complement test, not the fix.

**Second result: the unpriced default is now the ceiling.** 52.10bp is above every symbol we can
actually price (WETH 22.24, AERO 33.27). The change made the two symbols that are 20.6% of ticks
cheaper and left the other 93% exactly where they were, so the priced-vs-unpriced admission gap went
from zero to 19–30bp, opening in the direction that refuses the unpriced. A universe restriction
arriving by cost curve instead of by filter — slower and harder to see than the one the criterion was
written to prevent. Filed `[5ebe7c64]` with a held-out test as the kill condition: if 52.10bp sits
near the middle of what the other 8 census symbols predict for a held-out 9th, the complement wins

**Third: three census scripts now report a default as a measurement.** `ghost_gate_forensics.py:205`,

### Pass 462 addendum: it is FOUR cost reads, not two, and two of them cannot see a symbol

I ran the end-to-end trace I had just written into `[fa681912]` as work for somebody else, because
the item was unresolvable without it. **One AERO round trip, four live call sites, 13.1x apart:**

| call site | cost | source | symbol-aware? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `services/atf_static_strategy.py:880` | 33.27bp | census | yes — migrated |
| `services/symbol_edge_gate.py:476`, `strategy_edge_gate.py:288` | 46.13bp | DB-measured | **no — signature is `(*, db_path)`, it cannot take one** |
| `trading/bot.py:2235` | 52.10bp | census | **no — passes no symbol, gets the unpriced default** |
| `trading/scheduler.py:1800` | 435.00bp | token table | yes |

**The symbol-aware cost project is 2 of 4 done and the denominator was never known to be 4.**
`[84e62c6d]` is correct and verified, but it migrated one module. It could not have fixed
`symbol_edge_gate` (needs a signature change) or `bot.py:2235` (needs a caller change, tracked as
`[5454d2dd]`). `bot.py:2235` is the dangerous one: it imports the *new* module, so it reads as
migrated to anyone grepping imports, and silently takes the unpriced default.

**THE SPREAD INVERTS BETWEEN TOKENS, so do not average the four.** On AERO the census is cheaper
than the token table (33.27 vs 435.00); on WETH the token table is cheaper (11.00 vs 22.24). Any
reconciliation that splits the difference helps one token and hurts the other. Price WETH through
all four before touching a line.

**Already diagnosed once, in our own source.** `trading/bot.py:2231`: *"when each carried its own
copy of the formula they disagreed silently — the scout charged no fee at all."* That is this
defect at function scale, fixed once by consolidation. It returned at module scale, and the
per-symbol fix is what let it return — it removed the shape difference that used to make the two
modules obviously different things. **Consolidation is not durable unless the names say what each
thing measures.**

**Closed / not closed:** the *measurement* is closed — four numbers, named lines, reproducible. The

looks more carefully derived. All four look carefully derived; that is how we ended up with four.
