### Pass 462, CORRECTION: my own AERO slippage number was ghost-diluted by 7.6x — 22.04bp, not 2.89bp

I wrote the caveat ("the table mixes live and ghost rows; ghost fills cannot carry slippage; a
ghost-heavy average is biased down") about *other* symbols and then quoted 2.89bp for AERO anyway.
Applying my own caveat to my own number:

```
AERO-USDC   n=122   exact-zero rows=106   nonzero rows=16   mean over NONZERO only = 22.04bp
```

**106 of 122 AERO rows are `executed_price == expected_price` — ghost.** They dragged the mean from
22.04 to 2.89. **The caveat I wrote was the defect in the number I wrote it under.**

**Corrected:** AERO full round trip = 33.27bp census floor + round-trip slippage on 22.04bp/leg ≈
**55–77bp**, depending on whether 22.04 is a leg or a trip — *not established, not guessed*. Against
the 435bp `scheduler.py:1800` charges that is **~6–8x too strict, not the ~11x I claimed.** The
conclusion survives; the margin does not. `TOKEN_ROUND_TRIP` is still convicted on AERO.

**And the CBETH 198bp outlier I flagged is dead — killed, not left hanging.** Distribution:
`0.0bp ×46`, then **one row at exactly 10000.0bp**, then 60.1, 31.4, 16.2, 13.5. A single row at
exactly 100% deviation sets that mean — a unit/denomination bug, not a fill. **One row sets the
sign**, the pattern this repo has shipped repeatedly. Do not open an item on CBETH. AERO's 16
non-zero rows top out at 63.7bp with no such artifact, which is why AERO's corrected number stands
and CBETH's does not.

**The transferable rule, and it is the most useful thing in this pass:** *split live from ghost
before computing any cost statistic on `trade_fills`.* 87% of AERO's rows are ghost and **every one
of them reads as a perfect fill**, so any naive average over that table is biased toward zero cost —
the direction that makes trading look cheaper than it is.

## Pass 463 — the permutation bar is anti-conservative (Echo, senior)

**Route:** audit the null that `scripts/predicate_forge.py` scores every predicate
against, before building the second null `[fa1e7361]` asked for.

**Finding:** the null already exists — `permutation_bar()` at line 344 — but line 367
is `yp[idx] = yp[rng.permutation(idx)]`, an **i.i.d. shuffle within symbol**. It
destroys serial dependence that the real series carries.

Pre-registered kill test: if |rho| is inside the 2/sqrt(n) band at every lag, the
i.i.d. shuffle is defensible and the item should be rejected. Measured on the exact
forward-return series the function shuffles (168h, 30,895 ticks, 68 symbols):

| horizon | n | band | lag1 | lag2 | lag3 | lag4 | lag5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2m | 21,690 | ±0.0136 | +0.2856 | +0.1161 | +0.0940 | +0.0565 | +0.0471 |
| 3m | 23,827 | ±0.0130 | +0.3939 | +0.1364 | +0.0938 | +0.0659 | +0.0417 |
| 5m | 26,514 | ±0.0123 | +0.5461 | +0.2720 | +0.1672 | +0.1155 | +0.1015 |
| 8m | 27,254 | ±0.0121 | +0.5562 | +0.3281 | +0.2085 | +0.1507 | +0.1136 |
| 12m | 27,477 | ±0.0121 | +0.6339 | +0.4638 | +0.3323 | +0.2386 | +0.1718 |

Every cell outside the band; lag-1 at 12m is 52x it. Crude n_eff = n(1-rho)/(1+rho)
= 0.23n at 12m, so the bar is computed as if 4.4x more independent observations
existed — roughly **2x too narrow in SE terms**. The script's printed 4.65bp and
13.72bp bars are floors, not bars.

**The caveat that keeps this honest:** rho rises monotonically with horizon
(0.29 → 0.63 as 2m → 12m), the signature of **overlapping forward windows**, not
necessarily market memory. I cannot separate the two here and do not claim to.
It does not change the conclusion: the real series has the dependence and the
shuffled one does not, so the fix (block bootstrap) and the direction of the
error (anti-conservative) are identical either way. Overlap makes it worse, not
better, because overlap is guaranteed rather than contingent.

**Status: OPEN, not closed.** `[fa1e7361]` refined with these numbers and line
references rather than rejected. Reproduce: import `predicate_forge`, call
`load_ticks(168.0)` then `build_features`, autocorrelate `fwd[H]` within `sid`.

**Also measured this pass, unrelated and both worth carrying forward:**
- `[f6055c6b]` **EXISTS** (commit `4ab7a48`). The standing "do not restart
  production until it lands" block is **satisfied and was stale**.
- `scripts/live_lane_refusal_census.py` **contradicts itself**: prints
  `is_live_approved(money_button_dip) = True`, then a NOTE below concludes it
  returns False. The NOTE predates `f211df8` and was never updated.
- `data/strategy_ledger.json` holds **one** entry, `money_button`. `money_button_dip`
  **is not in the ledger at all** — its approval is inherited by alias, never granted.
- Same census, §5: `EXECUTE_LIVE_TRADES` and `LIVE_TRADES_DRY_RUN` both unset, so
  the dry-run default wins — **the executor is in DRY RUN**. Approved and armed
  still places no order.

### Pass 463 addendum — the correction is measured, not estimated: 1.7x to 2.6x

The `n_eff` argument above predicted the bar is "roughly 2x too narrow in SE
terms". That was an analytic estimate. Measured it directly instead, by a second
and independent method: hold ONE fixed predicate (`r6` top-quintile, the
momentum-shaped one), and compare the sampling SD of its lift under the i.i.d.
within-symbol shuffle `predicate_forge.py:367` uses against a **circular block
shift** within symbol, which preserves serial structure. 300 resamples each:

| horizon | n(P) | SD i.i.d. | SD circular | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2m | 4,197 | 0.41bp | 0.69bp | **1.69x** |
| 3m | 4,609 | 0.45bp | 0.81bp | **1.78x** |
| 5m | 5,147 | 0.49bp | 1.07bp | **2.16x** |
| 8m | 5,326 | 0.52bp | 1.28bp | **2.44x** |
| 12m | 5,398 | 0.63bp | 1.63bp | **2.59x** |

**The shipped null is 1.7–2.6x too narrow, rising with horizon**, and the 12m
figure (2.59x) lands on the independent `n_eff` prediction (~2x). Two methods,
one answer.

**Two caveats that bound the claim.** A circular shift is not a block bootstrap —
it preserves structure but resamples nothing, so it is a *lower* bound on how
much a proper block bootstrap would widen things, not a drop-in. And this is ONE
fixed predicate, whereas the shipped bar is a **max over a whole screen**; the
max statistic need not scale by the same factor as a single lift. So read
1.7–2.6x as the size of the effect, not as a correction factor to multiply the
published bars by. Getting the real number is `[fa1e7361]`.

Reproduce: scratchpad `bar.py`, read-only, imports `predicate_forge` without
modifying it.

### Pass 465 RETRACTION -- "the same fourteen" was a coincidence

I argued the ledger's win counter tracks **gross** profit because the ledger holds
14 wins of 20 and my ops-row count gave 14 of 21. **Retracted.** I never checked
that the row sets were the same rows. One query:

    scout ghost-exit ops rows, all time        126
    ledger ghost book, same strategy           253 trades

**The ledger holds twice as many trades as there are ops rows to build it from**,
so it cannot be derived from them and no count match across the two is a join.
Over all 126 ops rows the gross is **+2.0502 with 112 wins (88.9%)** — matching
neither the ledger's 199/253 (78.7%) nor its +6.6802.

Worse, the cost field is **not missing at random**. Of 126 rows only 21 carry
`roundtrip_cost_usd`, and those 21 are **81% VIRTUAL-USDC (17 of 21)** while the
105 without it are AERO 26, BSTONK 20, CBBTC 13, BASECAT 12, CBXRP 11, CBETH 9.
So the net-of-cost census I ran is 83% incomplete **and** symbol-skewed — which
matters a great deal here, because AERO and WETH sit at opposite ends of this
chain's cost wall.

**WHAT SURVIVES:**

- The scoreboard reads the ledger's tradeable subset — an exact digit-for-digit
  match on `0.12070961597995647` and 14/20, not a count coincidence.
- `199 + 13 = 212` against `trades = 253`. Internal to one file, needs no join.
  `[99728b37]` stands.
- The gross/net mechanism at `ledger.py:804` and the two writers are real.

**WHAT DOES NOT:** that this strategy's book was written gross. Unproven.
`[4c267abe]` criterion 3 is **fully open**, and neither known writer produces
+0.1207 — so a third writer or a third quantity exists.

The lesson is one my own memory index already carries and I walked into anyway:
**a matching count across two books is not a join.** The n=21 kill test that
closed the scout-promotion route is unaffected — it compared `profit` against
`roundtrip_cost_usd` **within each row**, never across books.

### Pass 465 final -- the third writer, and a caveat on my own kill test

**THE THIRD WRITER IS `services/atf_static_strategy.py:140`**, the scout's own
module: `StrategyLedger().record(strategy_id, profit=float(profit),
mode="ghost", symbol=symbol, held_sec=...)`. Its docstring says why it exists:
*"This loop runs its own ghost cycle rather than going through `bot.py`'s exit
path, which is the only other place that calls `StrategyLedger.record()`. Without
this the outcomes were written to `trading_ops` and nowhere else: 196 closed
trades over four days that the graduation gate never saw."*

So there are **three** writers into the ledger, not two, and the scout's 253-trade
book comes from its own module — neither `bot.py:10834` nor the backfill. Folded
into `[4c267abe]` and `[d5fbddfc]`.

**CAVEAT ON MY OWN NUMBER, same file, line 970:**

    "roundtrip_cost_usd": _roundtrip_cost_usd(clip_usd)      # NO symbol

The symbol-aware two-arg form is used twelve lines earlier at `:880`
(`_roundtrip_cost_rate(clip_usd, symbol)`) and is **not** used for the field
written onto the row. So the cost stamped on every evidence row is the
**symbol-blind constant** — this is
[[roundtrip-cost-rate-is-blind-to-the-token-and-gates-entries]] surfacing inside
the evidence book, and it is why the field reads ~0.0232 on a 6.0 clip on every
token.

**Therefore my 19.0% net win rate is not precise.** It is computed against a
symbol-blind cost, and for VIRTUAL-USDC (81% of the 21 rows) the true round trip
could sit either side of it. I should not have described it as "the cost it
recorded itself" without saying what that cost is made of.

**THE ROUTE STAYS CLOSED REGARDLESS, and that is the point of having had two
criteria.** The first needs no cost model: **gross is −0.0203, already negative
before anything is subtracted.** A strategy that loses money gross is not
rescued by a better cost estimate. The conclusion survives the defect I just
found in its own input.

GIL-holding thread (3 of 6 dumps) is `production.py:609` —

detach=True)`. Its own comment records someone already catching it starving the
feed: *"dataset_warmup timed out 28 times and held 93.4s per 10 minutes — 15.6%
of the whole queue"* (6h, 2026-09-11). The fix applied was `detach=True`.

**Detaching removes it from the scheduler QUEUE, not from the GIL.** A detached
thread running `json.loads` holds the interpreter lock exactly as hard as an
attached one, and the asyncio loop cannot run a callback while it does. The queue
symptom was fixed and the stall was not — which is why that comment reads as
solved while the feed still goes dark. Up to 2 min of GIL pressure per 10 min,
from a **model** task, under a header saying model work must never cost trading —
serving a brain that is `OMEN_STRATEGY_ENABLED=0`, closed negative.

measured blackout. Confirm the correlation before changing anything; if
dataset_warmup is *not* holding during the blackouts, the socket read (2 of 6) is
the better suspect. On `a2bfd079`.

dl-dynamic 4, seq-dataset_warmup 3, asyncio_9 1, resource-governor 1 (+2
ssl_wrap_socket, 1 fetch_trades, not GIL-marked). `dl-dynamic` appears *more*
than dataset_warmup and was absent from the first six samples entirely.

**What survives all twelve: the GIL is almost never held by the trading loop.**
The asyncio supervisor thread was active ONCE in twelve dumps. Everything else
was a model task, a download thread, the resource governor, or a TLS handshake.
This process is not blocked by a single culprit — it is **GIL-contended by a
crowd**, and the money path is one voice in it.

That may change the fix shape entirely: *"find the blocking call"* and *"the
trading loop shares an interpreter with a dozen model/IO threads and loses"* have
very different answers — a bugfix versus a process split. **Take substantially
more than twelve samples, inside measured blackouts, before choosing.**

## Pass 479 (Echo) -- [eb269198] AUDITED, NOT SHIPPED. THE ITEM NAMES THE WRONG MECHANISM.

I re-ran the previous passes' zero-delivery claim instead of inheriting it, and
it REPRODUCES on a fresh 7-day window -- but I found two things the item has
wrong, and I did not ship the change because neither the restart nor the 6-hour
census fits in a 30-minute pass.

FIRST, THE WRONG TABLE WILL FOOL YOU. `prices` holds 44 rows ALL TIME and
carries none of these sources (consensus/coinpaprika/coinlore only). The tape is
`market_stream` (116,805 rows), and the source lives inside its `raw` JSON under
the key **`rest`**, not `source`. A pass that queries `prices` concludes every
endpoint is dead, including the ones that work.

    market_stream by `rest`, last 7d:
      dexscreener   16149
      geckoterminal  9189
      kucoin         9099
      bitstamp        475
      okx/bybit/mexc/kraken/coinbase   0
      TOTAL         34912

Third window, third pass, never inverted. CONFIRMED.

SECOND, `_WS_POOL` IS NOT A WEBSOCKET POOL. It is a ranking table, read only by
`_ranked_endpoints()` (trading/data_stream.py:2511-2526). Every endpoint --
pool member or not -- is polled over REST by the same loop, which stamps
`"rest": endpoint.name` at :1311. All 34,912 rows carry that key and none carry
a websocket marker. Membership only ranks an endpoint FIRST. So the real defect
is sharper than the title: the five dead endpoints are polled BEFORE the four
that answer.

THIRD, AND IT CHANGES WHAT THE FIX BUYS: removing a name does NOT stop polling
it. `rank()` falls through to `base + _FALLBACK_PREFERENCE.get(name, 10)`. With
pool=("kucoin",), base=1, so okx/bybit/mexc/kraken/coinbase rank 11 while
dexscreener ranks 5. They are demoted below the sources that deliver, not
deleted. Expect LATENCY TO FIRST GOOD TICK to improve; do NOT expect the ~7560
polls to disappear. Any pass claiming a poll-count saving must measure it.

CLOSED: "delete the five endpoints and save 7560 REST timeouts" as written.
OPEN: the one-line demotion, which is still correct and still priority 3.
I rewrote the item's acceptance criteria with all three corrections rather than
filing a new id.

## Pass 480 (Echo, senior) -- [46145c10] THE HORIZON AXIS IS CLOSED. Shortening the hold makes it MONOTONICALLY WORSE, and "the book is positive inside 15 min" is an exit-reason tautology.

ROUTE TRIED: extend the horizon sweep BELOW 12 min -- the only band never
tested. Standing-instruction route (c), "SHORTEN THE HOLD", rests on it.

COMMAND: scripts/money_button_edge_terms.py HORIZONS extended from
(12,20,30,45,60,90) to (2,3,5,8,12,20,30,45,60,90); `python -X utf8
scripts/money_button_edge_terms.py --hours 168`. 148 symbols, 34,955
evaluations, 0.70% round trip.

RESULT -- NEGATIVE, AND MONOTONE. Up-rate (share of sequential windows whose
gross clears the 70bp round trip), null population:

    2min  3.0% | 3min  3.6% | 5min  4.3% | 8min  5.1% | 12min  6.4%
   20min  8.6% | 30min 11.9% | 45min 14.2% | 60min 15.8% | 90min 21.0%

Strictly increasing in horizon. The bleed does NOT shrink below 12 min; it
GETS WORSE, and the horizon that minimises it is the LONG end (60 min, net
mean -0.3637% on the guarded `aligned` population), not the short end. My
pre-registered hypothesis was that cost is fixed while adverse drift
accumulates, so the minimum sits at 2 min. That is DEAD.

WHY, and it is not subtle: the median net is pinned at exactly -0.700% =
-cost for every horizon at or below 45 min, i.e. THE MEDIAN GROSS MOVE IS
EXACTLY ZERO. At 66.6s median sampling a 2-min hold is ~2 ticks and adjacent
returns share a price print. Cost is fixed per round trip; the move scales
with sqrt(time). Short holds pay the same 70bp toll on a smaller move.

NOTHING CLEARS THE BAR ANYWHERE. Max lift at any horizon is +0.0385% =
3.85bp (60 min). The bar is 11bp. So the criterion "any candidate over 11bp
must survive --exclude-recent-hours 168" is satisfied VACUOUSLY -- there is
no candidate to hold out, and re-screening the classical set "at the best
short horizon" is moot because no short horizon is best at anything.

DO NOT TRUST THE NULL MEANS AT 2/3/5 MIN: +1590%, +1943%, +2604%. Those are
denomination-break / two-regime contamination, and it is WORSE at short
horizons, not better. The guarded `aligned` and `clean` populations read
-0.77%, -0.78%, -0.76% at the same cells. Judge this table by the UP-RATE,
which is a rate and immune to outlier magnitude.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT DIRECTION -- and this one explains the belief that sent
me here. "The tradeable book is POSITIVE inside 15 minutes and negative
after" is NOT hold-duration causation. It is the exit rule naming the
outcome. Win rate by exit reason over trade_outcomes:

    take_profit_limit   n=18   win 100.0%   sumnet +3.3060
    timed-exit          n=55   win   0.0%   sumnet -1.4421
    confidence_drop     n=72   win  43.1%   sumnet +0.1725
    negative_margin     n=17   win  11.8%   sumnet -0.4196

A take-profit exit is a winner BY CONSTRUCTION and fires EARLY. A timed exit
is the position that never hit its target, BY CONSTRUCTION, and fires at max
hold. 100% vs 0% is not a finding about time, it is a tautology about naming
-- and it corroborates the existing note exit-reason-name-decides-whether-it-
books. (The +3.3060 is additionally suspect per ghost-take-profit-fills-past-
its-limit; I did not re-audit it and did not need to.)

CONSEQUENCE: shortening the hold cannot convert a timed-exit loser into a
take-profit winner. It cuts the position off earlier, with a smaller move,
against the same toll -- which is exactly what the up-rate column measures.

STATUS: CLOSED. The horizon axis is exhausted in both directions -- pass 427
closed 12-90 min out-of-sample, this closes 2-12 min. Route (c) of the
standing instructions is refuted and should stop being offered as a live
option. The cost floor (70bp round trip against a median gross move of ZERO)
is the binding constraint, and it is a TOKEN/DEPTH problem, not a timing one.

 1. momentum_not_aligned is the REFUSED population. It is not a strategy, it

    ON THE TAPE, not an edge anybody can trade. Quoting it as a strategy
    result would be exactly the kind of artifact this repo keeps producing.
 2. Its up-rate is 51.9%, a coin flip. A +9.53bp gross mean at 51.9% up is

CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: on this tape there is no positive-expectancy
configuration visible at any horizon (2-90 min) or at any depth we can reach.
Cost reduction is necessary and insufficient. The missing term is GROSS, and
gross is a SIGNAL/UNIVERSE problem -- which tokens actually move more than
their own toll -- not a timing or clip problem.

This is consistent with, and independent of, pass 478's book-wide finding
(de-contaminated gross -0.0744% of notional vs a +0.3187% variable floor).
Different instrument, different window, same sign.

### Pass 480, fourth measurement -- I EXTENDED PAST 90 MIN AND THE RESULT IS A TRAP. h* FALLING WITH HORIZON IS ARITHMETIC, NOT EDGE -- AND PRODUCTION CANNOT HOLD PAST 45 MIN ANYWAY.

I said above that nobody had measured past 90 min and mean|move| was still
rising. I measured it. Same method, HZ extended to 120/180/240/360/480:

    sym     n      cost_bp  best_hz  mean|mv|bp   h*
    CBBTC   200    14.5     360      689.2        0.511
    WETH    1265   4.1      480      122.2        0.517
    AERO    2646   10.1     480      215.6        0.523
    CBETH   200    67.1     180      449.3        0.575
    VIRTUAL 905    67.6     480      246.7        0.637
    VVV     599    212.5    480      556.1        0.691
    DRB     503    1507.6   480      551.3        PERFECT ORACLE LOSES
    COMP    140    3301.5   180      542.2        PERFECT ORACLE LOSES

WETH h* 0.559 at 90 min becomes 0.517 at 480 min. That looks like the answer.
IT IS NOT, AND I AM RECORDING IT AS A TRAP RATHER THAN A RESULT.

WHY IT IS ARITHMETIC. Cost is FIXED per round trip; |move| grows roughly as
sqrt(t). So h* = 0.5 + cost/(2*mean|move|) falls monotonically toward 0.5 as
the horizon grows, FOR ANY COST WHATSOEVER, including an absurd one. DRB and
COMP only fail because their cost is so large the tape ran out before the
sqrt caught up. This metric therefore CANNOT be used to choose a horizon --
it always prefers the longest one measured, by construction. Anyone quoting
"you only need 51.7% accuracy at 8 hours" has quoted a tautology.

WHAT IT LEAVES INTACT: nothing here says a predictor exists. h* is the bar,
not a score. The measured up-rate on the populations our gates actually
select is 51.9% -- a coin flip -- and an 8-hour forecast is not obviously
EASIER than a 90-minute one. h* falling says the bar drops with horizon; it
says nothing about whether anything clears it.

AND THE CONSTRAINT THAT ENDS THE DISCUSSION FOR NOW -- production cannot
reach these horizons at all:

    .env:169  MAX_HOLD_FORCE_SECONDS=2700        (45 min)
    .env:138  ATF_STATIC_GHOST_MAX_HOLD_SEC=2700 (45 min)

The reachable ceiling is 45 MINUTES. Every horizon in the table above from
90 min upward is unreachable without an operator knob change. At the best
REACHABLE horizon the pass-480 sweep measured up-rate 14.2% and net -0.5850%.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE HORIZON AXIS, final: 2-90 min is closed on measurement
(monotone, all negative). 90-480 min is open only in the sense that the BAR
falls there, which is arithmetic, and it is unreachable in production today.
Extending MAX_HOLD_FORCE_SECONDS is an OPERATOR decision with a real cost --
[the-cost-gate-is-disabled-for-long-holds] records that the cost gate is
already switched off past 45 min -- and it should not be changed on the
strength of a tautology.

n SHRINKS AS THE HORIZON GROWS (CBBTC 286->200, COMP 233->140) because long
windows run off the end of a 168h tape. The longest cells are the thinnest.

The answer was already in this repo, committed ONE DAY before I filed the

commit (4.9x, 5.3x, 0.49x = 1/2.03). Same phenomenon, stated as settled.

MECHANISM, and it explains the CBBTC inversion I could not account for: the
legacy numbers came from the ROUTER PROVIDER, which picks the best tier PER
LEG INDEPENDENTLY and therefore CROSSES TWO POOLS. Same-tier quoting is what
makes a number a genuine round trip. A per-leg optimiser can land cheaper OR
dearer than a same-tier round trip depending on the token's tier structure,
which is why the error is not a uniform scale factor.

CORROBORATED BY LIVE FILLS, which outrank every quote in this repo: AERO
census 0.101% against 10.8bp MEASURED FROM ACTUAL FILLS; CBETH 0.603-0.617%
against 62.4bp measured. CBBTC does NOT corroborate (14.8bp quoted vs 2.2bp
filled) and by the artifact's own rule the QUOTE is the suspect there.

standing instruction reproduced in EVERY briefing --

    "AERO is the most-traded ghost symbol and costs more per round trip than

## Pass 481 (Echo, senior) -- RETRACTION: the 1.665 GB WAL is 0.06% live, and the "checkpoint copies 1.66 GB" line above (~L10877) is WRONG

**Route tried:** [c720dcdc], "checkpoint the 1.55 GB WAL, prime suspect for the
33% of event-loop samples parked ACQUIRING a db connection."
**Result: the premise is REFUTED. CLOSED as a latency route.**

I pre-registered the hypothesis and its complement before measuring:

* **H** -- the WAL is a stale **high-water mark**: live frames are a tiny
  fraction of the file, checkpoints are completing, nothing here stalls the loop.
* **C** -- the WAL genuinely holds 1.665 GB of un-checkpointed frames. Item stands.

**Kill test** (read-only parse of the WAL frame headers; no sqlite call, so it
cannot disturb the live writer -- production PID 22264 confirmed attached by
`tasklist` first):

    page size                  : 4,096          frame size 4,120
    capacity (frames on disk)  : 404,077
    checkpoint sequence number : 121        <- 121 completed checkpoint+restart cycles
    LIVE frames  (current salt):     225  =    0.9 MB
    STALE frames (stale salt)  : 403,852  = 1586.8 MB
    LIVE FRACTION              : 0.0557%

**H wins.** Every load-bearing claim fails:

1. **"388x (or 406x) past its own checkpoint threshold."** The *live* WAL is
   **225 pages against a 1000-page threshold = 0.23x**. It has not *reached* the
   threshold. Only the dead file is 404x, and dead frames are copied by nothing.
2. **"A checkpoint copies 1.66 GB under a write lock."** A checkpoint copies
   **225 frames = 0.9 MB**. Autocheckpoint is *working*: sequence number 121.
3. **"CONFIRMED AND GETTING WORSE, up from 1.55 GB" (pass 458)** -- a **GiB-vs-GB
   unit error**. `1,664,797,272` bytes = **1.5505 GiB = 1.6648 GB = 1587.7 MiB**,
   the same number three ways. The filing used binary; pass 458 divided raw bytes
   by 1000^3 and read the difference as growth. Passes **455, 458 and 481 all read
   1,664,797,272 exactly** -- zero growth in three days of production.

**Cause NAMED** (the original DONE criterion demanded one): it did **not** grow
unbounded. It grew **once** and stayed, because SQLite rewinds a WAL in place
after checkpoint and never truncates it unless `journal_size_limit` is set --
and it is unset (default -1). **Dead disk, not a live checkpoint cost.**

**Consequence for the open question:** the **33% of py-spy samples parked in
`__enter__` acquiring a connection is UNEXPLAINED AGAIN.** A 0.9 MB checkpoint
cannot produce a multi-second stall. The paragraph above that concludes "on this
evidence it is a cause" is **retracted**. Surviving suspects: connection-pool
exhaustion behind a long-held connection, and the standing finding that the loop
is ~90% blocked on a **synchronous socket read**. Anyone re-attributing this to
the WAL must first re-run the frame parse and show live frames in the *hundreds
of thousands*.

**What replaced it -- [1706fe9e], and it is a bigger risk than the item it came
from:** `df -h /d` reports **895G size, 880G used, 15G avail, 99% full**, holding
a **25.9 GiB** actively-written `storage/trading_cache.db`. If that volume fills,
production *stops* and a partial write into a 25.9 GiB store is how sqlite
corrupts -- taking the only on-chain evidence this loop has. **The growth rate is
UNMEASURED**, which is the first acceptance criterion rather than the remedy. The
safe reclaim is one line -- `PRAGMA journal_size_limit` beside the existing
`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` at `db.py:89`, applied at the **next planned restart**,
never a blocking `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` against the money path.

**Closed:** the WAL as a latency cause. **Open:** the 33%, and the disk.

Chased from the rejected WAL item. All read-only (`mode=ro`, `query_only=1`);
readers never block a WAL writer, and production (PID 22264) stayed untouched.

**Attribution** -- 800 random rowid *lookups* per table (B-tree point queries,
not scans), accounting for **98% of the 25.93 GiB file**:

    22.38 GiB  organism_snapshots   337,469 B/row x  71,204 rows   <- 86%
     2.43 GiB  kv_store             156,398 B/row x  16,692 rows
     0.26 trading_ops | 0.13 metrics | 0.07 feedback_events
     0.02 GiB  market_stream    ~0.00 system_logs, trade_fills

**The trading evidence is 0.02 GiB.** `trade_fills` ~1,124 live rows. It is not
the problem and a prune aimed at `organism_snapshots` cannot harm it.

**The writer is LIVE:** newest snapshot **17 minutes** old; 122 rows in 1h,
7,235 in 24h, 24,945 in 7d (**35% of the whole table**). Deleting without
stopping it refills the disk. The brain it serves is **paused and closed
negative** (`OMEN_STRATEGY_ENABLED=0`).

**Rate, two independent methods, 5% apart** -- this kills the short-window
objection I raised against myself earlier in the pass:

    A  raw file size, 12.5 min apart : 1.264 GB/day -> 12.6 days headroom
    B  7d row count x sampled size   : 1.203 GB/day -> 13.2 days
       (24h window, pessimistic      : 2.442 GB/day ->  6.5 days)

**Two measurement traps recorded, both of which I fell into first:**

1. **`MAX(rowid)` misreads this database by up to 800x.** `system_logs` shows
   max rowid 6,246,951 but only **~7,808 rows exist** -- the rest are deleted
   ids. My own "system_logs is 90% of rows, prune the logs" reading came from
   this and is **wrong**; pruning logs reclaims ~0.00 GiB.
2. **A modulo-sampled row length is not a byte estimate.** My first attempt
   returned `n=2` rows for the biggest table and implied 1.8 GiB of content in a
   25.93 GiB file -- i.e. "it's mostly free pages, VACUUM reclaims 24 GiB".
   `freelist_count` = **192 pages, 0.0% free** refuted it outright. **That route
   is CLOSED.**

**VACUUM order is a trap:** an in-place VACUUM needs ~25.9 GiB free against
14.78 GiB available. Use `VACUUM INTO` a new file, production **stopped**, then
swap. `auto_vacuum=0`, so freed pages never return on their own.

**Open, on `[1706fe9e]`:** stop the snapshot writer (the actual fix), then
reclaim at a planned restart. Operator's call -- not taken.

  much as halving the window -- inspect one payload first.

**Unchanged, because it was measured rather than inferred:** the 25.93 GiB
attribution (86% this table, 98% of the file accounted), 0.02 GiB of trading

### Pass 484 addendum 8 -- TRULY FINAL. My own headline ask was wrong, and the
### constriction is one layer lower than the whole quote thread.

**THE TRIM ASK IS DEAD, corrected in the same pass I made it.**
`MID_TOKENS['base']` (`services/providers/uniswap_v3.py:140`) is exactly TWO
entries -- WETH and cbBTC -- and `.env` has no UNIV3 override. So the 2-hop
search is 2 mids x 16 fee pairs = 32 eth_calls plus ~8 direct = ~40 total.
There is nothing to trim: halving a two-element list discards half the routing
on base, and the two entries are the intermediates anyone would choose.

**~40 eth_calls in 45s is ~1.1 SECONDS PER CALL.** A healthy node answers 40
eth_calls in a few seconds. That is a SLOW OR RATE-LIMITED RPC, not an
expensive search.

**I COULD NOT TIME IT AND DID NOT ESTIMATE IT.** There is no base RPC URL in
`.env`; the only RPC-ish keys are `PREFER_FREE_RPC` and `WIZARD_NODE_URL`, and
neither is an http endpoint for base. The URL resolves somewhere I did not find
in the time. The timing loop is STILL OPEN.

**But `.env:15` reads `PREFER_FREE_RPC=1`.** Free public base endpoints are
aggressively rate-limited, and a throttle presents as exactly what was
measured: ~1s per call, consistent, with no fast failures anywhere. CONFIG FACT
PLUS A FITTING HYPOTHESIS -- NOT A MEASUREMENT. The complement is live: the RPC
may be fast and something in the provider may be serialising or retrying.

If the free-RPC reading holds, ONE cause explains everything found today -- the
87% symbol loss, the 45s wall, the ~3.0 hours/day of burned quote budget, and
CBADA failing 3 quotes in 4. Unlike every route closed this pass, it has a
cheap fix that is not a code change.

NEXT, IN ORDER (all on [b6be1b81]):
  1. Find where the base RPC URL resolves -- NOT `.env`, already checked.
  2. Time 40 sequential eth_calls. Near 45s => the RPC is the whole story;
     a few seconds => look inside the provider.
  3. Only then price a paid base endpoint, and put the number in front of the
     operator rather than provisioning anything (AWS is down; cost matters).

pre-filter, and the trim-the-mid-tokens ask that was my own report's headline.

DESIGN. Pairing is the whole point. This tape drifts and entries arrive in

not what the gate knew. Every comparison is made inside a 10-minute window
holding at least one accept AND one refuse; only the within-window difference is
aggregated, so drift is common to both arms and cancels. 7 days, 59 accepts

priced symbols from `market_stream`.

| 180m | 29 | +70.82 bp | [+21.44, +120.19] | 72.4% |
| 360m | 24 | +134.02 bp | [+23.29, +244.76] | 79.2% |

with the refused pool running the OTHER way over the same horizons (90m
-17.76 bp, 180m -14.00 bp). An 85 bp separation at 180 min, 3x the cost floor,
up-rate rising monotonically 50% -> 79%.

IT IS NOT REAL. The paired, drift-controlled version, swept over the pairing
window:

| horizon | window | windows | paired diff | 95% CI | acc won |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 90m | 600 | 24 | +6.11 | [-46.02, +58.24] | 41.7% |
| 90m | 1800 | 25 | -9.29 | [-56.80, +38.23] | 44.0% |
| 180m | 600 | 17 | -31.34 | [-114.40, +51.71] | 41.2% |
| 180m | 1800 | 17 | -23.02 | [-97.92, +51.88] | 52.9% |
| 360m | 600 | 13 | +77.98 | [-42.26, +198.22] | 69.2% |
| 360m | 1800 | 17 | -50.70 | [-172.86, +71.47] | 52.9% |

Every one contains zero, and **the sign flips on an arbitrary bucket width I
chose myself**: 90m goes +6.11 -> -9.29, 360m goes +77.98 -> -50.70. At 180 min
the paired diff is negative in both. The unpaired lift is the tape rising in
the windows where entries happened to cluster -- accepted and refused sit in
different symbols at different times, which is precisely the artifact the
pairing was built to remove.

CLOSED: **do not lengthen the hold.** It is the obvious action from the
unpaired table and it is unsupported. `MAX_HOLD_FORCE_SECONDS=2700` (.env:169)
is not what is costing us. The coin-flip verdict now stands over 15m to 360m
rather than 15m to 45m.

METHOD NOTE worth more than the result: the unpaired table would have passed
review -- it has n, CIs excluding zero, a monotone up-rate, and a control arm
running the other way. It is still wrong. The only reason it was not published
as a finding is that the kill test was pre-registered, so running it was not a
choice made while excited about the number.
